name: Oak Steakhouse
desc: Charleston-born steakhouse at Avalon known for dry-aged beef, Wagyu and ribeyes, backed by an extensive wine list. One of Alpharetta's go-to special occasion rooms.
tips: Reserve ahead for Friday and Saturday dinner; online reservations are offered on the restaurant's site.
Sunday dinner starts at 4pm and the prime rib special runs only until it sells out, so go early.
Ask about the private dining spaces if you are planning a group celebration or business dinner.
about: Oak Steakhouse brings a modern take on the classic American steakhouse to Third Street in Avalon. The kitchen centers on Certified Angus Beef, with cuts such as the filet, New York strip and bone-in ribeye, alongside seasonal seafood, house-made pastas, locally inspired sides and nightly specials. Wet-aged and dry-aged steaks are also sold for shipping nationwide.

The room mixes leather banquettes and exposed brick with a glowing open kitchen, and guests can choose the main dining room, the bar or one of the private spaces. The restaurant pitches itself for celebrations and business dinners, and its wine list and cocktail program are a big part of the draw. Sundays bring a prime rib special served until it sells out, plus oyster and wine deals.

Oak is run by The Indigo Road, a hospitality group with Oak locations across the Southeast, including the original in Charleston. The Alpharetta restaurant has appeared on steakhouse lists from Atlanta Magazine and Eater Atlanta.

name: South City Kitchen Avalon
desc: Upscale Southern cooking at Avalon, known for fried chicken, biscuits, shrimp and grits and one of the area's most popular brunches.
hours: Breakfast Mon-Fri 7-10am; Lunch Mon-Fri 11am-2pm; Brunch Sat-Sun 8am-2pm; Dinner Mon-Thu 5-9pm, Fri-Sat 5-10pm
about: South City Kitchen Avalon is the Alpharetta branch of the long-running South City Kitchen concept, which is known for elevated Southern cooking. The Avalon restaurant sits at The Hotel at Avalon on Avalon Boulevard and serves breakfast, lunch and dinner on weekdays plus brunch on Saturday and Sunday.

The menu pairs familiar South City Kitchen signatures with seasonal, chef-driven Southern dishes that Avalon's directory describes as exclusive to this location. Expect a polished, sit-down setting that works for a hotel breakfast meeting, a business lunch or a weekend brunch with family.

Avalon's directory notes that the bar stays open later on weekends. Because it is part of the hotel, the restaurant is an easy choice for visitors staying at Avalon as well as locals who want a Southern meal before shopping or a show nearby.
tips: Book brunch ahead on weekends, when it is one of Avalon's busier meals.
Weekday breakfast starts at 7am, which makes it a handy spot for an early meeting.
Park in any of Avalon's free garages and walk over to the hotel.

name: Rumi's Kitchen
desc: Persian dining at Avalon known for juicy kabobs, fragrant rice and hummus. A metro Atlanta favorite that made Avalon a food destination.
about: Rumi's Kitchen at Avalon serves Persian cooking from chef Ali Mesghali, who grew up in Esfahan, Iran and Los Angeles before building his career in Atlanta. The restaurant group also runs locations in Sandy Springs, Colony Square, Washington DC and Houston, and the Avalon dining room opened in 2017 in the second phase of the development.

Expect a lively room with high, sweeping ceilings, an open kitchen and a busy bar. The restaurant says it has the largest outdoor patio at Avalon, which makes it a popular pick for lunch or dinner outdoors while shopping, and it has become a regular choice for celebrations and business meals.

Rumi's offers a private dining space for groups as well as off-site catering for events ranging from small home gatherings to weddings. Online ordering and gift cards are available through the restaurant's website.
tips: Park free in one of the two Avalon garages directly behind the restaurant, or use Avalon's valet near the concierge booth.
Ask for the patio on a mild evening; it is the largest at Avalon.
Reserve ahead for groups and celebrations, or inquire about the private dining room.

name: Colletta
desc: Northern Italian at Avalon with wood-fired pizza and house-made pasta in a lively dining room.
about: Colletta is a modern American Italian restaurant at Avalon whose name means "collection" in Italian. The from-scratch kitchen makes its own pastas and cheeses, cooks over wood fire and turns out Neapolitan-style pizza along with red sauce classics, with the menu shifting through the seasons.

The dining room is lively and built around an open kitchen. Besides the full a la carte menu, Colletta offers a nightly "For the Table" option, a chef-curated family-style meal meant for passing plates around a group. The bar program leans on Italian wines, spritzes and aperitivo culture, and happy hour runs at the bar on weekday evenings.

Colletta is part of The Indigo Road group, which also runs Oak Steakhouse a few doors away, and has locations in other states. Weekend brunch is served Saturday and Sunday, and private dining spaces are available for corporate events and family celebrations.
tips: Try the family-style "For the Table" menu if you are dining with a group.
Weekday happy hour at the bar runs from 5 to 6pm.
Brunch is served on weekends from 11am to 2:30pm; book ahead for larger parties.

name: Antico Pizza
desc: The Avalon outpost of Atlanta's famed Neapolitan pizzeria, with blistered wood-fired pies, gelato and cappuccino.
hours: Mon-Thu 11am-9pm; Fri-Sat 11am-10pm; Sun 11am-8pm (closes when dough runs out)
about: Antico Pizza's Avalon shop is part of the Little Italia family of restaurants founded by Giovanni "Gio" Di Palma, whose original Antico opened in Atlanta's West Midtown in 2009. The pizzeria built its name on Neapolitan-style pies baked in wood-fired ovens with traditional, high-quality ingredients.

The Avalon location uses a shared menu with Antico's Battery and Tucker shops. It is a casual, order-and-eat pizzeria rather than a reservation restaurant, and the company only takes special reservations for parties of 10 or more, based on availability.
Pickup and delivery can be ordered through Antico's online partners. Antico also ships frozen pizzas nationwide through Goldbelly, which makes it a common gift choice for out-of-town fans.
tips: Walk in for a regular meal; reservations are only taken for parties of 10 or more.
For a large group, email the events team or call the Avalon shop directly to request a reservation.
Order ahead online for pickup on busy weekend nights.

name: Superica
desc: Ford Fry's Tex-Mex cantina at Avalon, known for chorizo queso fundido, sizzling fajitas and a popular Sunday brunch.
hours: Lunch Mon-Fri 11am-3pm; Dinner Mon-Thu 3-10pm, Fri 3-11pm; Brunch Sat-Sun 10am-3pm
about: Superica is chef Ford Fry's Tex-Mex cantina, and its Avalon location sits on 1st Street in Alpharetta. The menu covers lunch, dinner and weekend brunch, with nachos, tacos, fajitas, enchiladas and margaritas in a colorful dining room styled after the Old West. Fry's Tex-Mex cookbook is sold through the restaurant's website.
Lunch runs on weekdays, dinner starts at 3pm, and brunch is served Saturday and Sunday from 10am to 3pm. Takeaway, online ordering and catering for pickup are all available.

For groups, Superica can seat up to 30 people for dinner in a semi-private space or up to 40 on its covered patio. The patio can also be closed for a private cocktail event for up to 60 guests, and full buyouts are possible through the Rocket Farm Restaurants events team.
tips: Weekend brunch starts at 10am, so arrive early to beat the late-morning rush.
Ask about the covered patio for a group dinner of up to 40 guests.
Order catering ahead for pickup if you are hosting a party at home.

name: The Cape Restaurant & Beach Bar
desc: Cape Town-inspired coastal restaurant at Avalon with a sunset rooftop and a crab dip locals rave about.
about: The Cape Restaurant & Beach Bar is a coastal restaurant at Avalon inspired by the cooking and wines of Cape Town, South Africa. It is part of True Story Brands, the group led by South African restaurateur Justin Anthony, and it replaced the group's Biltong Bar at Avalon in 2021.

The all-day menu leans on bold, global flavors. Signature dishes include a fried whole red snapper with pickled pico de gallo, cilantro coconut sauce and peri-peri sauce, pan-seared halibut with red butter curry over coconut rice, tuna tartare and ostrich sliders with house fries.

Inside, the dining room is decorated like a beach bungalow with surfboards, colorful pillows and hanging plants. Upstairs, a covered rooftop patio with its own bar overlooks Avalon Boulevard and works well for cocktails or larger groups. The restaurant is open seven days a week and hosts private events.
tips: Ask for a rooftop table for views over Avalon Boulevard; the patio is covered.
Try a South African touch such as the ostrich sliders or a peri-peri dish.
Contact the restaurant through its website for private events at the beach bar.

name: MF Bar
desc: Sushi rolls, nigiri and a deep sake list served around a big U-shaped bar at Avalon.
about: MF Bar is a Japanese-inspired restaurant on Avalon Boulevard from the team behind Atlanta's MF Sushi. The menu centers on hot and cold small plates, with sushi rolls and nigiri as the main attraction.

The drinks list matches the food, with cocktails built to pair with the dishes and a wide selection of sake. Avalon's directory describes the focus as quality ingredients, authentic flavors and attentive service, and it places the restaurant in the higher price range among Avalon's dining options.

It suits a date night or a relaxed dinner with friends who want to share several plates. Avalon residents and office tenants can arrange delivery through the Avalon concierge, and questions can be sent to the restaurant by email.
tips: Order a mix of hot and cold small plates to share, then add rolls or nigiri.
Ask for a sake recommendation to go with your sushi.
Park in an Avalon garage; parking at the development is free.

name: CRU Food and Wine Bar
desc: Wine bar at Avalon with build-your-own cheese flights, shareable plates and a people-watching patio.
about: CRU Food and Wine Bar sits in the center of Avalon Boulevard and offers a list of more than 350 wines. Guests can order premium wines by the glass or a red or white flight, which is a tasting of three related wines grouped by grape, region or style.

The food menu is built to pair with the wine, with shareable appetizers, individual gourmet pizzas, entrees and a selection of imported and domestic cheeses. The setting is elegant but casual, with a sunny patio for happy hour and a rooftop deck overlooking The Plaza for evenings out.

CRU was established in 2002 in Texas and is part of a Dallas-based restaurant company founded by restaurateur Patrick Colombo, with locations in several states. At Avalon it is close to the valet stand and the concierge desk.
tips: Order a wine flight if you want to compare three related wines.
Head to the rooftop deck for people-watching over The Plaza.
Use Avalon valet or the free garages; the restaurant is near the concierge desk.

name: Barleygarden Kitchen & Craft Bar
desc: Gastropub at Avalon with 60+ craft beers on tap, burgers and sandwiches and a dog-friendly patio.
about: Barleygarden Kitchen & Craft Bar is a beer-focused restaurant at Avalon from the Hop City group. Both the downstairs bar and the rooftop pour a curated mix of North American craft beers and European favorites, and the staff will help you find your next pint.

The kitchen sources locally when possible and cuts its own beef and pork. The menu moves from pub staples such as fish and chips, wings, a fish sandwich and a buffalo chicken wrap to vegan and gluten-free choices. A to-go window and online ordering make it easy to grab a quick lunch or dinner.

The restaurant has a casual patio, and Avalon's open-container setting lets guests stroll with a drink. With a rooftop bar and a menu made for sharing, Barleygarden is set up for birthdays, rehearsal dinners and corporate parties, which can be booked through its website.
tips: Head up to the rooftop bar on a nice evening.
Use the to-go window or order online when you are short on time.
Book group parties ahead through the restaurant's party request form.

name: Branch & Barrel
desc: Craft cocktails and elevated American fare at Avalon, known for the corn fried lobster sandwich and crispy Brussels sprouts.
about: Branch & Barrel is a craft bar and kitchen at 4100 Avalon Boulevard with a 19th-century industrial look. Avalon's directory names Todd Hogan as its chef, and the kitchen stresses scratch cooking, buying locally when it can, from cheese and vegetables to bread baked daily.

Cocktails get the same attention as the food. The bar makes its own shrubs, orgeat, mixers and bitters for its signature drinks, and bourbon is a particular focus, with a Bourbon Club that guests can join through the restaurant.

The restaurant sees itself as a neighborhood eatery inside Avalon, good for lunch, a date night or drinks with friends. It sits in the upper price range for the development and is open daily, with later hours on Friday and Saturday. Avalon residents and office tenants can arrange delivery through the Avalon concierge.
tips: Ask your bartender or server about joining the Bourbon Club.
Open until 11pm on Friday and Saturday, so it works for a late dinner after a show.
Park free in an Avalon garage and walk over.

name: Ted's Montana Grill
desc: Bison specialist at Avalon known for its 50/50 beef-bison burger and classic American comfort plates.
about: Ted's Montana Grill at Avalon is part of the restaurant chain co-founded by Ted Turner and George W. McKerrow. Bison is the cornerstone of the menu, and the company says it serves more bison than any other restaurant in the world, alongside beef and classic American dishes.

The restaurants are designed to look like 19th-century saloons, and small touches such as a bowl of half-sour pickles on the table are part of the routine. The chain's bison are ranch-raised on grass, finished on grain and never given hormones or steroids. A gluten-free menu plus online nutrition and allergen tools help guests plan around dietary needs.
The company also highlights sustainable choices such as paper straws and support for local growers. It is a relaxed, family-friendly option at Avalon for lunch or dinner.
tips: Call the Avalon restaurant directly to ask about reservations.
Check the gluten-free menu and allergen tool online before you go.
Online ordering is available if you prefer takeout.

name: Cafe Intermezzo
desc: Paris-style bistro and coffeehouse at Avalon with towering dessert cases, crepes, tarts and late-night espresso.
about: Cafe Intermezzo has brought the European coffeehouse tradition to the Atlanta area since 1971, when founder Brian Olson was inspired by bakery-cafes in Germany and Austria. The Avalon cafe is one of four locations, alongside Midtown Atlanta, Dunwoody and Nashville.

The menu covers specialty coffee, cappuccino, hot chocolate, cocktails and a large selection of tortes and cheesecakes, plus breakfast, brunch, lunch and dinner. Some breakfast items are served all day, and the pastries come from the company's own Epic Bakery, where whole cakes can be ordered for celebrations.

Outdoor covered seating is available year-round, and the cafe stays open until midnight on Friday and Saturday, which makes it a common stop for a late dessert. The Georgia Restaurant Association honored the company with its Grace Award for Hospitality Hero of the Year in 2023 for its charitable giving.
tips: Seating is first come, first served with no reservations, and parties on the wait list are limited to 5 guests.
Bring a card or exact cash, since the cafe does not keep a cash drawer.
Park in Avalon's free lots; the Whole Foods lot is not part of Avalon parking.

name: Jeni's Splendid Ice Creams
desc: Beloved scoop shop at Avalon with inventive flavors and fresh waffle cones.
about: Jeni's Splendid Ice Creams runs a scoop shop at 800 Avalon Boulevard. The ice creams are made from scratch using a recipe that founder Jeni Britton has refined over more than 20 years, with a smooth texture and flavors inspired by art, history and pop culture.

Alongside classic flavors, the shop rotates seasonal and limited releases, and Jeni's makes a full line of dairy-free flavors for guests who avoid milk. Pints, gift boxes and other take-home items are also sold through the company.

The Avalon shop keeps late hours, open until midnight Sunday through Thursday and until 1am on Friday and Saturday, so it is an easy stop after dinner at one of the nearby restaurants or a show. Jeni's also offers local delivery and a fundraising program in the Atlanta area.
tips: Ask about the dairy-free flavors if anyone in your group avoids dairy.
It stays open late, so save room for a scoop after dinner at Avalon.
Check the Jeni's app or website for local delivery and seasonal flavors.

name: Smokejack Southern Grill & BBQ
desc: Southern BBQ in a historic brick building on Main Street, known for hand-pulled pork, ribs and beef burnt ends.
about: Smokejack Southern Grill & BBQ is a barbecue restaurant at 29 S Main St in downtown Alpharetta, in a historic brick building on Main Street. It is known for Southern barbecue such as hand-pulled pork, ribs and beef burnt ends.

Its downtown location puts it within walking distance of City Center and the other Main Street restaurants. Check the restaurant's website or call ahead to confirm current hours and menu before visiting.
tips: Call ahead to confirm hours before you go.
Downtown parking can fill on weekends, so allow time to find a space.
Combine a meal with a walk around Alpharetta City Center nearby.

name: The Butcher and Bottle
desc: Chef-driven steakhouse with Southern roots on Roswell Street in downtown Alpharetta, part of a small north Georgia restaurant group that also runs other Butcher & Bottle locations. It focuses on upscale steaks and Southern plates with handcrafted drinks, in a walkable spot near City Center.
tips: Plan on dinner rather than lunch, since it operates as an evening restaurant.
Downtown parking fills on weekends; the City Center decks are a short walk away.
Call ahead to confirm hours and reservations.
about: The Butcher and Bottle is a chef-driven steakhouse with Southern roots at 45 Roswell St in downtown Alpharetta. It is part of a small north Georgia restaurant group with other Butcher & Bottle locations, and the menu focuses on steaks and Southern plates with handcrafted drinks.
The restaurant sits in a walkable part of downtown, a short distance from Alpharetta City Center. It runs as an evening dinner spot, so plan accordingly and call ahead for current hours.

name: The Southern Porch
desc: Fried green tomatoes, pimento cheese and biscuits and gravy served on a breezy screened-in porch downtown.
about: The Southern Porch is a breakfast and lunch spot at 62 N Main St in downtown Alpharetta. Its menu leans on Southern comfort dishes such as fried green tomatoes, pimento cheese and biscuits and gravy, served on a breezy screened-in porch.
Listed hours run from 8am to 2pm daily, which makes it a daytime stop for a downtown breakfast or an early lunch. Hours and menu should be confirmed with the restaurant before visiting.
tips: Go early on weekends, when daytime spots downtown get busy.
Ask for a seat on the screened porch on a mild morning.
Confirm hours on the restaurant's website before heading out.

name: Citizen Soul
desc: California cuisine with a Southern accent in the heart of downtown.
about: Citizen Soul describes itself as "a soul from the South with an eye on the West." The restaurant at 60 South Main Street takes its cue from pubs and taverns in Northern California, Oregon and Washington, serving California cuisine with Southern heart built on simple, fresh ingredients.

It is an upscale but casual neighborhood eatery with modern American pub fare. The bar is a big part of the visit, with artisanal cocktails, craft beer on tap and a wine collection that leans heavily on California and other domestic producers.

Dinner is served every night, with earlier starts on Saturday and Sunday. Reservations are taken through Resy, and private events can be booked through the restaurant's event page. Online ordering and gift cards are also available.
tips: Book a table on Resy, especially for Friday and Saturday dinner.
Ask the staff for a pick from the California wine list.
Saturday service starts at 2pm, handy for a late lunch downtown.

name: Hen Mother Cookhouse
desc: Homemade comfort food and baked goods downtown; a staple for breakfast and brunch.
about: Hen Mother Cookhouse is a breakfast and brunch restaurant at 50 S Main St in downtown Alpharetta. It is known locally for homemade comfort food and baked goods and has been a regular stop for breakfast and brunch downtown.
Listed hours run from Tuesday through Sunday in the morning and early afternoon, with the restaurant closed on Mondays. Because hours can change, check with the restaurant before you go.
tips: Plan a visit Tuesday through Sunday, since it is closed Mondays.
Arrive early on weekends for brunch.
Confirm current hours by phone before heading downtown.

name: Up On The Roof
desc: Rooftop brunch above downtown with mimosa carafes, bayou crab cakes and challah French toast.
hours: Mon-Thu 3pm-12am; Fri 3pm-2am; Sat 11am-2am; Sun 11am-12am; brunch weekends from 11am
about: Up On The Roof is a rooftop restaurant and bar at 33 S Main St in downtown Alpharetta, part of a small group with other rooftops in Greenville and Anderson, South Carolina. It serves dinner, late-night drinks and weekend brunch with views over downtown.

The menu runs from shareable small plates and appetizers to seasonal entrees and desserts, with handcrafted cocktails and seasonal drinks at the bar. The restaurant is minutes from Avalon and Ameris Bank Amphitheatre, so many guests stop in before or after a concert.

The rooftop hosts seasonal events such as holiday dining, a Christmas pop-up bar and brunch with Santa. Large party seating and private dining are available, and the restaurant offers delivery and online ordering. It opens in the afternoon on weekdays and earlier on weekends.
tips: Reserve a table online for weekend brunch or a pre-concert dinner.
It stays open until 2am on Friday and Saturday for late-night drinks.
Ask about large party seating or private dining for celebrations.

name: Maple Street Biscuit Company
desc: Flaky biscuit sandwiches with inventive fillings, served downtown.
about: Maple Street Biscuit Company serves handcrafted breakfast and lunch from 50 Canton St in downtown Alpharetta. The chain opened its first restaurant in Jacksonville, Florida in 2012, later moved its headquarters to Nashville and now operates in several states.

Biscuit sandwiches built around hand-breaded chicken are the core of the menu. The Squawking Goat, with fried chicken, crispy goat cheese and pepper jelly, was featured on Food Network's "Guilty Pleasures," and other favorites include the Five and Dime with bacon, cheddar, egg and gravy, plus hash bowls, waffles and cold brew.
The restaurant is a daytime spot, opening at 7am every day and closing in the early afternoon. Online ordering and catering are available through the company's website.
tips: Order ahead online to skip the line on weekend mornings.
Try the Squawking Goat if it is your first visit.
Weekend hours run an hour later, until 3pm.

name: Crust Pasta & Pizzeria
desc: Tuscan-style antipasti, pasta and pizza on South Main Street.
address: 131 S Main St, Ste H, Alpharetta, GA 30009
about: Crust Pasta & Pizzeria is a South Main Street Italian restaurant led by chef Darren Henderson. The menu covers antipasti such as calamari, mussels and arancini, soups and salads, pastas, pizzas and desserts like tiramisu and creme brulee.

The kitchen makes a lot in house. Fresh egg pasta and ravioli are made daily in the pasta room, pizza dough and garlic knots are made fresh each day, and the sauces, dressings and even cannoli shells are house-made. Beef and pork come from hormone and antibiotic free sources and are ground in house for meatballs and Bolognese.
Gluten-free crust is offered for pizzas, and the restaurant runs a catering menu with family-style trays for pickup or delivery. It is a casual pick for a family dinner downtown.
tips: Ask for the 10-inch gluten-free crust if anyone in your group avoids gluten.
Give 24 hours notice for catering pickup and 72 hours for delivery.
Start with the garlic knots, which are made fresh in house daily.

name: Fogon and Lions
desc: Spanish, Latin American and Caribbean-inspired plates and drinks just off the Town Green.
about: Fogon and Lions celebrates Spanish and Latin flavors around its namesake fogon, a traditional wood-burning kitchen where food is cooked over open flame. The menu ranges from steaks, seafood, ceviches and churrascos to cheeses, cured hams, tacos and whole roasted meats.

The restaurant is owned by chef Julio Delgado, a Food Network "Cutthroat Kitchen" winner and Georgia Grown Executive Chef for 2019, and his wife Zoribeth Delgado, who is from Juana Diaz, Puerto Rico. For groups, the kitchen offers a whole roasted suckling pig, cochinillo asado, cooked over the wood fire and carved at the table for 10 to 12 guests.
It sits at 10 Roswell Street just off the Town Green, with a public parking garage right next door. A happy hour menu and private events are also offered.
tips: Park in the Alpharetta public garage next to the restaurant.
Order the cochinillo asado in advance for a group of 10 to 12.
Lunch is served Wednesday through Sunday; Monday and Tuesday open at 4pm.

name: Cabernet Steakhouse
desc: Club-like steakhouse and seafood room on Windward Parkway with a deep wine list; an Alpharetta institution.
hours: Lunch Mon-Fri 11:30am-4pm; Dinner Mon-Thu 5-9pm, Fri-Sat 5-10pm; Sun closed
about: Cabernet Steakhouse calls itself Alpharetta's original steakhouse and marked 25 years on Windward Parkway in 2025. Modeled on the classic steakhouses of New York, it serves prime meats and seafood prepared simply, along with a deep list of wines and spirits.
The large dining room has high ceilings, rich woods and plush seating, and it looks onto an open stainless steel kitchen. The dress code is business casual, with no athletic wear or ball caps.

Lunch is served on weekdays and dinner Monday through Saturday, and the restaurant is closed on Sundays. On Friday and Saturday nights it offers a three-course prix fixe menu, and it hosts periodic wine tasting events. Reservations are encouraged and can be made through its website.
tips: Reservations are encouraged, especially for weekend dinners.
Dress business casual; athletic wear and ball caps are not allowed.
Ask about the weekend three-course prix fixe.

name: Pampas Steakhouse
desc: Argentinian-style steakhouse cooking over wood embers on a custom grill.
address: 10970-A State Bridge Rd, Johns Creek, GA 30022
about: Pampas Steakhouse serves Argentinian-style steaks on State Bridge Road in Johns Creek, a short drive from Alpharetta. Steaks are cooked the traditional Argentinian way, over an oak wood fire and a bed of hot coals.

Specialties include "The Brick" filet, a bone-in filet and cuts such as the tomahawk, Delmonico and churrasco. The wine list has repeatedly earned Wine Spectator's Best of Award of Excellence, and the restaurant cites recognition from Zagat and OpenTable.

The wood-paneled setting includes a bar, a main dining room and several private dining rooms for banquets and events, with a private dining coordinator on staff. The bar is an option for a more casual visit. Pickup and delivery orders are available online.
tips: Book a table online, especially for weekend dinners.
Contact the private dining coordinator for group events.
Order The Brick filet, one of the house specialties.

name: Vinny's on Windward
desc: Longtime Windward Italian known for risotto, gnocchi and tiramisu.
about: Vinny's on Windward describes its cooking as California Italian, fresh and lighter than traditional red sauce fare. It is part of the Sedgwick Restaurant Group, the Alpharetta company behind Pure Taqueria and Theo's Brother's Bakery, which supplies artisan breads.

Specialties range from seared big eye tuna with pinzimonio salad and beef carpaccio to wood oven pizzas, rack of lamb, veal or chicken scallopini and tiramisu. The restaurant says it has been rated "Excellent" by Zagat and that its wine list has earned praise from Wine Spectator.

Vinny's has served Windward Parkway for about two decades and pitches itself as a lunch spot for local business people and a date night destination. Lunch, dinner, dessert and aperitivo hour menus are posted online.
tips: Reserve through the Sedgwick Restaurant Group website.
Weekend service starts at 4pm, so plan lunch visits for weekdays.
Order online for takeout through the restaurant's Toast page.

name: Ippolito's Family Style Italian
desc: Local Italian restaurant group serving north metro Atlanta since 1989, with a casual, friendly dining room on Highway 9 at Windward. The menu covers homemade sandwiches, pizzas, calzones and pastas, plus chicken, veal and seafood specialties, a broad wine list and desserts.
tips: Order carry-out for a family pasta night at home.
It opens at 11am daily, which suits an early weekday lunch.
Call ahead to confirm current hours.
about: Ippolito's Family Style Italian is a casual Italian restaurant on Highway 9 near Windward in Alpharetta. It belongs to a local restaurant group that has served north metro Atlanta since 1989, and its menu covers sandwiches, pizzas, calzones and pastas plus chicken, veal and seafood dishes, wine and desserts.
Carry-out is available for a family meal at home. Listed hours are daily from 11am, but confirm with the restaurant before visiting.

name: Nahm Fine Thai Cuisine
desc: Upscale Thai on Windward Parkway, run by chef Nahm Thongyoung since 2006.
address: 5310 Windward Pkwy, Ste C, Alpharetta, GA 30004
about: Nahm Fine Thai Cuisine on Windward Parkway was founded by Nahm Stamm, who grew up learning to cook from her grandmother, mother and aunt in Thailand and worked in hospitality at the Four Seasons there before moving to America. She opened the restaurant to give guests a truer taste of Thai cooking.

The menu covers Thai dishes, fresh seafood and hand-crafted cocktails, served in a polished dining room suited to intimate dinners, special occasions and corporate events. The restaurant says it has received recognition from Wine Spectator and OpenTable diners.
Lunch is served on weekdays and dinner every night. Private parties can be booked, and online ordering is available for pickup or delivery.
tips: Reserve ahead for a special occasion dinner.
Lunch runs weekdays only, 11am to 3pm.
Ask about private party bookings for group celebrations.

name: Secreto Southern Kitchen & Bar
desc: Farm-to-table Southern dishes on Windward Parkway.
about: Secreto Southern Kitchen & Bar is listed at 6195 Windward Pkwy, Suite 102, in the Windward area of Alpharetta. It has been described as a farm-to-table Southern restaurant.

Its listed website no longer shows restaurant content, so its current status could not be confirmed, and no hours are listed. Call the restaurant before visiting to make sure it is open and to check hours.
tips: Call before visiting to confirm the restaurant is open.
Ask about current hours, since none are listed.
Check for reservations by phone.

name: Tarahumata Mexican Grill & Tequila Bar
desc: Tarahumata Mexican Grill & Tequila Bar has served Windward Parkway since 2006, pairing Mexican and Tex-Mex plates with tapas-style small plates and a list of more than 150 tequilas. Popular picks include grilled hanger steak, calamari, tostadas, mini burgers and prawns, with seating inside or on the patio.
tips: Ask the bar about a tequila flight.
The patio is a good pick on mild evenings.
Call ahead to confirm hours.
about: Tarahumata Mexican Grill & Tequila Bar is a Mexican and Tex-Mex restaurant at 6195 Windward Pkwy in Alpharetta. It has been described as serving Windward Parkway since 2006, with tapas-style small plates and a list of more than 150 tequilas.
Menu picks have included grilled hanger steak, calamari, tostadas and prawns, with seating inside or on the patio. Confirm hours with the restaurant before visiting.

name: Curry Pizza House
desc: Curry Pizza House, paired here with Hidden Tap & Barrel, tops craft pizzas with Indian curries and spices, from tandoori chicken to paneer, alongside wings and a full bar. The Windward Parkway space has indoor and outdoor seating, and the menu includes several vegan pizzas made with gluten-free crust and vegan cheese.
address: 5530 Windward Pkwy, Ste C-300, Alpharetta, GA 30004
tips: Try the Curry Chicken Masala or Shahi Paneer pizza, the top sellers.
Order ahead online for pickup on busy nights.
Open until 11pm on Friday and Saturday.
about: Curry Pizza House tops craft pizzas with Indian curries and spices. The concept started in Fremont, California in 2012, created by first-generation Indian Americans who began adding their mother's curry to family pizza nights, and it has grown to several states before arriving in Alpharetta.

Signature pies include Curry Chicken Masala, Shahi Paneer and Tandoori Chicken, alongside classic pizzas. The company says its dough is made in the store and never frozen, and that vegetables are sourced fresh daily.

The restaurant sits at 5530 Windward Parkway and is open every day for lunch and dinner, with later hours on Friday and Saturday. The founders say they travel to European and Asian cities looking for new flavors. Orders can be placed online for pickup.

name: The Original Pancake House
desc: The pancake specialist, serving its famous apple pancake and Dutch baby on Windward Parkway.
about: The Original Pancake House on Windward Parkway has served scratch-made breakfast in Alpharetta since 2007. The brand dates to Portland, Oregon in 1953, and the local restaurant follows the same rule of making everything from scratch each day.

The signature Apple Pancake is oven-baked to order with a caramelized cinnamon glaze and takes close to an hour. Other favorites include the Dutch Baby, six-egg omelets, French toast and Swedish crepes. The kitchen uses high-grade butter, hand-cracked Grade AA eggs and fresh-squeezed orange juice.
It is a daytime restaurant, open from early morning into the afternoon every day. Lines are common on weekends, and online ordering and private dining are available.
tips: Order the Apple Pancake early, since it takes nearly an hour to bake.
Expect a line on weekend mornings and arrive near opening time.
Order online for pickup if you are short on time.

name: J Christopher's
desc: Breakfast, brunch and lunch standby at Windward Plaza.
about: J. Christopher's at Windward Plaza is part of a locally owned breakfast and lunch chain founded by Jay McCann and Chris Brogdon, which opened its first restaurant in Marietta in 1997. The company now runs restaurants across metro Atlanta, Macon, Savannah and Tennessee, including a second Alpharetta location on Old Milton.

The menu features what the company calls familiar food with flair: omelets, breakfast skillets, burgers, sandwiches and salads. House favorites include Blueberry Crunchcakes, Strawberry Waffles, Eggs Christopher and the Club House Burger, and seasonal menus rotate through the year.
The Windward restaurant is open every morning, closing at 2pm on weekdays and 2:30pm on weekends. Online ordering and catering are available.
tips: Order online for pickup to skip the weekend wait.
Try the Blueberry Crunchcakes, a house favorite.
Ask about catering for office breakfasts.

name: Luci's Ristorante Italiano
desc: Windward Italian steakhouse serving 35-day dry-aged cuts alongside classic pastas.
about: Luci's Ristorante Italiano on Windward Parkway blends Italian cooking with an American steakhouse. The kitchen focuses on fresh ingredients, family recipes and handmade pastas, and steaks are hand-cut and flame-grilled, with a 32-ounce tomahawk as the signature cut.
The menus cover dinner, wines by the glass and from the cellar, cocktails including zero-proof options, and beer. Happy hour runs at the bar on weekdays from 4 to 6:30pm.

Private dining is offered in the Toscana Room, the Roma Room and on an outdoor patio, with space for up to 54 guests, for holiday parties, rehearsal dinners, corporate events and milestone birthdays. The restaurant opens at 4pm Monday through Saturday, is closed on Sundays and recommends reservations on weekends.
tips: Reserve ahead for weekend dinners, as the restaurant recommends.
Catch weekday happy hour at the bar from 4 to 6:30pm.
Ask about the Toscana or Roma rooms for a private event.

name: Cooper's Hawk Winery & Restaurant
desc: Casual dining paired with a Napa-style tasting room pouring its own award-winning wines, on North Point Parkway.
about: Cooper's Hawk Winery & Restaurant on North Point Parkway pairs a full-service restaurant with a tasting room pouring the company's own wines. Guests can take a guided tasting at the bar, then sit down for lunch, dinner or weekend brunch.

A Wine Club gives members a wine of the month, dining rewards and discounts, and some membership levels include a monthly tasting for two. Weekday happy hour runs in the afternoon with cocktails, wines by the glass and small bites, and weekend brunch is served Saturday and Sunday mornings.
Carryout and curbside pickup are available, and the restaurant hosts private events. Gift cards and Wine Club gift memberships can be bought online or in the tasting room.
tips: Book dining reservations ahead; they are highly recommended.
Wine tastings are walk-in only and served in order of arrival.
Weekday happy hour runs from 3 to 5:30pm.

name: Food Terminal
desc: Malaysian street-food favorite in the North Point corridor, from the team behind the Atlanta original.
about: Food Terminal serves Asian street food with a strong focus on Malaysian cooking. It was founded by Amy, who began selling street-style noodles from a kiosk in Malaysia at 15, and Howie, who together also created Top Spice and Sweet Hut. The Alpharetta restaurant on North Point Parkway joins locations in Chamblee, West Midtown and Sandy Springs.

Malaysian food draws on Indian and several Chinese regional traditions, and the menu reflects that range. Favorites include garlic bone marrow noodle soup, Ipoh chicken hor fun, Hainanese chicken rice, roti canai, curry laksa and Hong Kong milk tea.
The menu is large, so it suits groups who want to share several dishes. Reservations are taken through Resy, and online ordering is available.
tips: Book a table on Resy for weekend dinners.
Order a few dishes to share, since the menu is wide.
Try the garlic bone marrow noodle soup, a signature.

name: Mama's Pizza
desc: Long-running North Point pizzeria known for New York-style pies and slices, plus Sicilian squares, stromboli, calzones, meatball subs and fresh salads. It has been at its North Point Parkway location since 2013 and is a regular pick among Alpharetta locals for a quick slice or a family pizza night.
tips: Try a Sicilian square pie for a change from the classic slice.
Call ahead for pickup on busy nights.
Confirm hours by phone, since none are listed.
about: Mama's Pizza is a North Point pizzeria at 5950 North Point Pkwy in Alpharetta. It is known for New York-style pies and slices, plus Sicilian squares, stromboli, calzones, meatball subs and salads.
It has been described as operating at its North Point Parkway location since 2013 and is a casual choice for a quick slice or a family pizza night. Confirm hours by phone before visiting.

name: Chronic Tacos
desc: California-style tacos, burritos and quesadillas near North Point.
address: 970 North Point Dr, Suite B160, Alpharetta, GA 30022
about: Chronic Tacos is a fast-casual Mexican grill at 970 North Point Drive, near North Point Mall and the GA 400 corridor. The company says its food is built on third-generation family recipes, with scratch-made rice and beans and house-made salsas.

The build-your-own menu covers tacos, burritos, bowls, quesadillas, nachos and loaded fries. Plates such as the two-taco plate come on corn or flour tortillas with your choice of protein, and specialty items include a surf and turf burrito with steak and shrimp.

It works well for a quick lunch break, a family dinner or office orders. Dine-in, takeout, online ordering, catering and a rewards app are available, and the restaurant is open from 11am to 9pm every day.
tips: Order ahead online or through the rewards app for a fast pickup.
Use the catering menu for office lunches.
Customize your plate with the build-your-own options.

name: Pappadeaux Seafood Kitchen
desc: Gulf Coast and Cajun seafood with a famous Sunday brunch, just off GA 400.
about: Pappadeaux Seafood Kitchen near North Point Mall serves Gulf Coast and Cajun seafood with Southern hospitality and French Quarter flavor. The restaurant sits on Davis Drive just off GA 400, close to North Point Mall, and is part of a chain with locations in several states.

The menu leans on Louisiana-inspired seafood, including crawfish dishes, along with Cajun favorites. It is a full-service, sit-down restaurant that works well for families, celebrations and larger groups.

Reservations are accepted, and private dining rooms are available for parties and business events. The Alpharetta menu is posted on the company's website. The restaurant opens at 11am daily and stays open later on Friday and Saturday.
tips: Make a reservation for weekend evenings.
Ask about the private dining rooms for groups.
It opens at 11am every day, which suits an early lunch.

name: Marlow's Tavern
desc: Neighborhood tavern known for its prime rib French dip, fish tacos and burgers.
about: Marlow's Tavern at Avalon is a neighborhood tavern serving scratch-made American food for lunch, dinner and drinks. The menus are led by chef John Metz, and tavern favorites include grilled Atlantic salmon and shrimp and grits.

The room has classic tavern seating and a few flat screens for watching the game without taking over the conversation. A patio offers outdoor dining with handcrafted cocktails, and a gluten-free menu and happy hour menu are posted online.

Marlow's has locations in Georgia and Florida, and the Avalon restaurant is at 3900 1st Street, open daily from 11am. Online ordering and catering are available, and an Insider Club offers rewards and event invitations.
tips: Grab a patio table on a nice day.
Check the gluten-free menu online before you go.
Join the Insider Club for offers and event invites.

name: Village Tavern
desc: Polished American tavern on Rainwater Drive with a big patio.
hours: Lunch Mon-Fri 11am-3pm; Brunch Sat-Sun 11am-3pm; Dinner Sun-Mon 3-9pm, Tue-Thu 3-10pm, Fri-Sat 3-11pm
about: Village Tavern is a polished American tavern at 11555 Rainwater Dr in Alpharetta. It is known for a large patio and serves weekday lunch, weekend brunch and dinner every day, according to its listed hours.
It is a sit-down option in the Windward and Rainwater Drive area for business lunches or relaxed dinners. Confirm hours with the restaurant before visiting.
tips: Ask for a patio table in good weather.
Weekend brunch runs late morning into the afternoon.
Call ahead to confirm hours and reservations.

name: Firebirds Wood Fired Grill
desc: American grill known for wood-fired steaks and seafood.
about: Firebirds Wood Fired Grill is an American restaurant and steakhouse at The Atwater on Old Milton Parkway, across from Avalon. The scratch kitchen is known for hand-cut, aged steaks and fresh seafood cooked over a wood fire, with crafted cocktails and a selection of wines.
The dress code is smart casual and reservations are recommended. The FIREBAR and patio host a weekday happy hour from 2 to 6pm with bar bites and drink specials.

Curbside pickup can be ordered online or by phone, and delivery is offered through DoorDash. The restaurant opens at 10am on weekends and stays open until 11pm on Friday and Saturday. A virtual tour of the dining room is posted on its website.
tips: Reserve a table, which the restaurant recommends.
Catch weekday happy hour in the FIREBAR or on the patio, 2 to 6pm.
Look for it in The Atwater at Old Milton Parkway and Westside Parkway.

name: Pure Taqueria
desc: Stylish Mexican spot known for seafood dishes and strong margaritas.
about: Pure Taqueria began in downtown Alpharetta in 2005, when longtime residents Chris and Michele Sedgwick opened it on the site of a 1920s Pure Fuel Oil station. The small stone building from the old station still stands on the property, though the restaurant itself was built new.
The menu is creative Mexican cooking with tortillas made in house daily and margaritas the brand is known for. The vibe is loud, lively and fun, and it has become a local institution.

The original has since grown into a franchise with locations across metro Atlanta, and the Sedgwicks' group also runs Vinny's on Windward. A catering menu serves all locations, and gift cards and online ordering are available.
tips: Order a margarita, a house specialty since the restaurant opened.
Expect a lively, noisy room on weekend nights.
Use the catering menu for parties and office events.

name: Delbar
desc: Middle Eastern favorite on Old Milton known for hummus, labneh, falafel and chicken kofta.
hours: Dinner Tue-Thu 5-9pm, Fri-Sat 4-10pm, Sun 4-9pm; Brunch Sat-Sun 11am-3:45pm
about: Delbar is a Middle Eastern restaurant at 4120 Old Milton Pkwy in Alpharetta. It is known for hummus, labneh, falafel and chicken kofta, and its listed hours cover dinner Tuesday through Sunday plus weekend brunch from late morning into the afternoon.
The Old Milton Parkway location is part of Delbar's small group of restaurants. Check with the restaurant to confirm hours and reservations before visiting.
tips: Book ahead for weekend brunch.
Plan around Mondays, which are not listed in its hours.
Confirm hours on the restaurant's website before you go.

name: Jerusalem Bakery & Grill
desc: Family-owned Middle Eastern bakery, grill and pizzeria on Old Milton Parkway, open since 2009, with shawarma, kebabs, hot sandwiches and breads baked in-house. A small market inside stocks spices, olives, rice, teas, tahini, cooking oils and cheeses for cooking at home.
address: 4150 Old Milton Pkwy, Ste 129, Alpharetta, GA 30005
tips: Pick up fresh pita or baklava to take home.
Order online to earn rewards points.
Ask about catering trays for office lunches or parties.
about: Jerusalem Bakery & Grill is a family-owned Middle Eastern restaurant and bakery on Old Milton Parkway, one of three locations along with Marietta and Roswell. The family says it brings more than 40 years of experience and also supplies its breads, pastries and sweets to other businesses across the Southeast.

The kitchen bakes pita and pastries in house and serves shawarma, kabob platters, falafel, lamb shank and sandwiches such as a Jerusalem cheesesteak. Baklava and other sweets are popular takeaway items.

The restaurant offers dine-in, takeout, delivery and outdoor seating, along with vegan options and a kids' menu. Catering is available for weddings, office lunches and family events, and a rewards program applies to online orders.

name: Efendi Mediterranean Restaurant
desc: Turkish Mediterranean restaurant that opened as Cafe Efendi in 2004 and rebranded as Efendi Mediterranean in 2026. The menu runs from hummus, falafel, kebabs and grilled seafood to lahmacun, Iskender and Turkish breakfast, and the space includes a cocktail bar, hookah lounge and enclosed patio.
tips: Visit for the weekday lunch specials, served 10:30am to 3pm.
Friday and Saturday nights bring a DJ and belly dancing; choose another night for a quieter meal.
Try the Turkish breakfast, which is meant for sharing.
about: Efendi Mediterranean Restaurant, formerly Cafe Efendi, has served Alpharetta from North Main Street since 2004. The menu mixes familiar Mediterranean dishes such as hummus, kebabs and falafel with Turkish specialties like lahmacun and Iskender, and a traditional Turkish breakfast with tea and coffee is served every day.

The space is set up as three areas: an upscale-casual dining room, a cocktail lounge and bar, and an enclosed outdoor patio used year-round. On Friday and Saturday nights a DJ and belly dancing performances run from 8pm until late.
Weekday lunch specials include a four-course lunch and a wrap special. The restaurant also hosts groups and private parties, and reservations and online ordering are available through its website.

name: Kailash Parbat
desc: North Indian and Sindhi cuisine on North Main Street.
about: Kailash Parbat is an Indian restaurant at 670 N Main St, Suite 110, on North Main Street in Alpharetta. It is described as serving North Indian and Sindhi cuisine, the latter from the Sindh region and less common on local menus.
No website is listed, so menu details and hours could not be confirmed. Call the restaurant before visiting to check hours and whether reservations are needed.
tips: Call ahead to confirm hours.
Ask staff for Sindhi specialties if you want something less common.
Check whether takeout is available when you call.

name: Sushi Sumo
desc: Neighborhood sushi and pan-Asian spot at Old Alabama Square.
address: 3005 Old Alabama Rd, Ste 440, Alpharetta, GA 30022
hours: Mon & Wed-Fri 11am-11pm; Sat 12-11pm; Sun 3:30-11pm; Tue closed
about: Sushi Sumo is a neighborhood sushi and pan-Asian restaurant at Old Alabama Square, a shopping center at 3005 Old Alabama Rd, Suite 440. Its listed hours run late most evenings, with the restaurant closed on Tuesdays.
It is a casual pick for sushi in the Old Alabama Road area. Check the restaurant's website or call before visiting to confirm hours.
tips: Plan around Tuesdays, when it is listed as closed.
Sunday service is listed as starting mid-afternoon.
Confirm hours before you go.

name: True Food Kitchen
desc: Health-driven menu of bowls, salads and lean proteins.
about: True Food Kitchen at Avalon serves a seasonal, whole-food menu based on the anti-inflammatory food pyramid developed by founder Dr. Andrew Weil. Bowls, salads and lean proteins sit alongside vegan-friendly and gluten-friendly choices.

The restaurant draws weekday lunch crowds from nearby offices, weekend brunch diners and family groups. A full bar pours craft cocktails and organic wines, and house-made drinks take the place of regular sodas on the menu.

The Alpharetta location has an outdoor patio with seating for more than 120 guests. It is at 2140 Avalon Boulevard in the heart of the development, with valet and self-parking at Avalon. Weekend brunch starts at 10:30am. Reservations are available on OpenTable, and catering, private dining and online ordering are offered.
tips: Reserve on OpenTable for weekend brunch.
Ask for the patio, which seats more than 120.
Use Avalon's valet or self-parking on site.

name: Valor Coffee
desc: Downtown Alpharetta's hometown roaster, with indoor and outdoor seating a block off Main Street.
about: Valor Coffee opened its first cafe at 44 Milton Avenue in downtown Alpharetta. Founded in 2016 by Ross Walters, Riley Westbrook and Ethan Rivers, the company's mission is to uplift people through coffee, and it also has a cafe in Dunwoody and sells beans and subscriptions online.
The menu pairs espresso drinks with flavored lattes, and pastries come from Maven, the group behind South Main Kitchen. Seasonal coffees rotate through the year.

The cafe is small, with about 25 seats inside plus a patio, and it aims for a social, upbeat feel with music and a friendly staff the company calls the Pit Crew. It is a block off Main Street, close to downtown restaurants and shops.
tips: Grab a patio seat if the 25 indoor seats are full.
Try a seasonal flavored latte.
Pick up a bag of beans to brew at home.

name: Warm Waves Coffee
desc: Cozy downtown coffee shop with comfortable seating and a short food menu.
about: Warm Waves Coffee is a specialty roaster based in Norcross with cafes in Alpharetta and Suwanee. The Alpharetta cafe puts every coffee the company roasts on bar, so you can order a pour-over, an espresso or a bag of beans to take home.

The company buys through import partners that work with the same farmers year after year, names each coffee's producer and region, and publishes what its producers are paid. Beans are roasted to order in small batches, and bags hold a full 12 ounces.
The downtown cafe opens at 7am on weekdays and 8am on weekends, closing at 5pm. Online ordering is available, and coffee subscriptions can be set up through the website.
tips: Order a pour-over to taste a single-origin coffee.
Order ahead online for a quick pickup.
Ask staff which current coffee suits your taste before buying a bag.

name: Brewable
desc: Nonprofit coffee cafe in the lobby of the Alpharetta Community Center that provides paid jobs for adults with intellectual and developmental disabilities. It serves hot and iced coffee drinks with quiche, scones and cake pops, and sells T-shirts and artwork, with a dog tie-up area outside.
tips: Grab a coffee before or after an activity at the Community Center.
Look for the T-shirts and artwork for sale at the counter.
Confirm hours before you go.
about: Brewable is a nonprofit coffee cafe in the lobby of the Alpharetta Community Center at 175 Roswell St. It provides paid jobs for adults with intellectual and developmental disabilities and serves hot and iced coffee drinks with quiche, scones and cake pops.
The cafe also sells T-shirts and artwork, and there is a dog tie-up area outside. Hours were not confirmed, so check before visiting.

name: Boarding Pass Coffee
desc: Airline-themed coffee shop complete with real Delta seating.
about: Boarding Pass Coffee is a travel-themed specialty roaster founded in 2020 by Murilo and Christine Santos. Some of its coffee comes from Fazenda Sant'ana, Murilo's family farm in Serra Negra, Brazil, and all of its beans are roasted locally in Georgia.

The downtown Alpharetta cafe opened in 2024 at Alpharetta City Center on Commerce Street, behind the fountain. Along with coffee drinks, it serves beer and wine. The company also runs a drive-thru on Old Milton Parkway, a roastery in Milton and cafes in Gainesville and Buckhead.
Orders can be placed for pickup or delivery, and bags of locally roasted coffee are sold to take home. The cafe stays open later on Friday through Sunday.
tips: Look for it behind the City Center fountain.
Order ahead for pickup through the website.
Visit Friday through Sunday for longer hours, until 6pm.

name: Fuel Coffee
desc: Industrial-style cafe on North Main with breakfast and lunch.
address: 800 N Main St Ste 110, Alpharetta, GA 30009
about: Fuel Coffee is an industrial-style cafe at 800 N Main St, Suite 110, on North Main Street in Alpharetta. The business operates as Fuel Coffee Roaster and serves breakfast and lunch alongside its coffee.

Its listed hours run from early morning into mid-afternoon on weekdays, with shorter weekend hours. The website offers online ordering for pickup. Confirm hours before visiting, since they could not be verified.
tips: Visit in the morning for breakfast with your coffee.
Weekend hours are shorter, especially Sunday.
Confirm hours before you go.

name: The Nest Cafe
desc: Lollipop waffles, croissants and beignets in downtown Alpharetta.
about: The Nest Cafe is a downtown Alpharetta breakfast, brunch and lunch spot at 58 Canton Street, open daily from 7am to 3pm. The menu is made to order, with an emphasis on wholesome options in a homey setting.

Sweet signatures include fluffy lollipop-style waffles, honey toast with vanilla gelato and beignets with a house chocolate dipping sauce. Paninis, a California club, turkey and brie, a Reuben and a Cuban come with a choice of sides, and the drinks menu includes seasonal lattes, dairy alternatives, fresh smoothies and gelato shakes.
After hours, starting at 4pm, the cafe hosts private events for up to 50 guests, such as baby showers and birthday parties. A mobile app handles ordering ahead.
tips: Order ahead in The Nest Cafe app and your food will be ready when you arrive.
Try the beignets with the house chocolate sauce.
Book the space after 4pm for a private party of up to 50.

name: Shibam Coffee
desc: Handcrafted drinks and light bites in the North Point corridor.
address: 4000 North Point Pkwy Ste 900, Alpharetta, GA 30022
about: Shibam Coffee is a Yemeni coffeehouse chain with a location on North Point Parkway in Alpharetta. The company is grounded in Yemeni coffee culture and pairs traditional drinks with a modern cafe setting meant for lingering and conversation.

The menu includes Yemeni coffees such as mufawar with milk and cardamom, Sana'ani, Jubani and qishr, a coffee-husk tea with ginger and spices, plus Adeni spiced milk tea, Saudi coffee and Turkish coffee. Black tea, Moroccan mint tea and ginger tea are also offered. Standard espresso drinks, pistachio and Spanish lattes, matcha and seasonal specials round out the list, along with pastries.
It keeps late hours, which makes it a popular evening meeting spot. Ordering is available through the Shibam app.
tips: Try an Adeni tea or mufawar for a traditional Yemeni drink.
Order ahead on the Shibam app.
It stays open late, so it works for an evening meetup.

name: Argentis Bakery
desc: Downtown bakery where everything is gluten- and dairy-free.
address: 42 Milton Ave Ste B, Alpharetta, GA 30009
about: Argentis Bakery is a dedicated gluten-free and vegan bakery in downtown Alpharetta. Every item is made without the top nine allergens, and the bakery describes itself as celiac-safe.

The case covers breads including artisan sourdough, cakes, cupcakes, cookies, muffins, pies, donuts and other pastries, along with coffee. Custom birthday cakes and wedding cakes are made to order, and tastings are available for couples planning weddings in the Atlanta area. Product listings online include items such as apple muffins and apple pie. An allergen guide on the website lists ingredients.
The bakery is open daily from 8am to 5pm, and orders can be placed online for pickup. It also sells its baked goods wholesale to other businesses.
tips: Order custom cakes at least 72 hours ahead.
Check the online allergen guide before you visit.
Ask about wedding cake tastings.

name: Vincent Bakery
desc: Korean bakery near North Point with pastries, boba and espresso.
address: 5950 North Point Pkwy Ste 129, Alpharetta, GA 30022
about: Vincent Bakery is a Korean-style bakery in the North Point area, listed at 5950 North Point Parkway, Suite 129. Alpharetta's visitor bureau describes it as a fresh Korean bakery serving baked treats alongside boba drinks and espresso favorites.

Think of it as a casual stop for a pastry and a drink rather than a sit-down meal. Current hours and a full menu could not be confirmed from an official source, so a quick call to (470) 814-2525 before a special trip is a good idea.
tips: Call ahead to confirm hours before making a special trip.
Pair a boba drink or espresso with one of the pastries.
It sits on North Point Parkway, handy before or after errands in the North Point area.

name: BB's Bagels
desc: Legendary bagels from a tin trailer on McFarland Parkway; go early, they often sell out.
address: 6835 Shiloh Rd E, Ste 4C, Alpharetta, GA 30005
about: BB's Bagels, also known as Bronx Bagels, is a family bagel shop that Anna and Eddie Siino opened in 2007 after years in baking and restaurant management in the New York and New Jersey area. The bagels are New York style, hand rolled and kettle boiled on site, and the shop is known for its lineup of cream cheeses and spreads along with breakfast sandwiches.

A fire on February 2, 2025 destroyed the original building on McFarland Parkway, and the bagel oven was the only thing the family salvaged. They reopened in August 2025 in a new space at 6835 Shiloh Road East, Suite 4C, close to the Shiloh Road and McFarland Parkway intersection.
The current shop is set up for takeout only, and it reopened with morning hours of 7am to 2pm, so plan on an early visit and enjoy your order at home or on the go.
tips: The shop moved after a 2025 fire; head to 6835 Shiloh Road East, not the old McFarland Parkway building.
It is takeout only, so plan to eat elsewhere.
Go in the morning; the shop keeps early hours and closes around 2pm.

name: Currahee Brewing Company
desc: Downtown taproom pouring Belgian golden ales, German lagers and coffee stouts; outside food welcome.
about: Currahee Brewing has been making beer since early 2016, with its main production brewery in Franklin, North Carolina, and taprooms in Alpharetta and Clayton, Georgia. The Alpharetta taproom on South Main Street sits right across from City Center, and the small brewhouse behind the bar is where the team produces test batches and one-off beers.

The lineup leans toward European-inspired ales and lagers. Regulars include Garand IPA, the Mountain Blonde ale and the Der Betrunken Oktoberfest, while Kawi, brewed with cold-brewed Nicaraguan coffee, took a bronze medal at the 2017 Great American Beer Festival.

There is patio seating out back and more outdoor seating up front. For food, Smokejack BBQ next door offers counter service, so you can grab barbecue without leaving the taproom area. The name comes from a Cherokee word roughly meaning "stand alone" and honors the 506th Infantry Regiment, which uses it as its motto.
tips: Grab barbecue from Smokejack next door to go with your beer.
Weekday hours start at 4pm; Friday and Saturday open at 1pm.
Check Currahee's Facebook events page for what is happening at the taproom.

name: Avalon
desc: Alpharetta's 86-acre upscale mixed-use district: dozens of shops and restaurants along the Boulevard, the Regal Avalon 12 theater, The Hotel at Avalon, and a plaza with bocce, swings and fire pits. Home to a seasonal ice rink, tree lighting and Santa visits each winter.
tips: Avalon on Ice runs from November 22 to January 18 this season.
Store and restaurant hours vary, so check a specific shop before you go.
Walk or bike the Alpha Loop, about a mile, to reach Downtown Alpharetta.
about: Avalon is a mixed-use district off Old Milton Parkway that blends shopping, dining, apartments, offices and The Hotel at Avalon. Stores and restaurants line the main Boulevard, there is a movie theater, and a concierge desk (770-765-1000) can help with directions and questions. General center hours run Monday through Saturday 10am to 9pm and Sunday noon to 7pm, though individual stores and restaurants set their own schedules.

Much of the appeal is the calendar. Each winter brings the Lighting of Avalon, Santa visits and Avalon on Ice, a Rockefeller-inspired skating rink that runs from November 22 to January 18 this season. Game-day gatherings and fall trick-or-treating are also part of the yearly lineup.

Avalon also anchors one end of the Alpha Loop, a paved trail that links it to Downtown Alpharetta in about a mile, and attractions such as Immersive Gamebox on 1st Street add things to do beyond shopping.

name: Downtown Alpharetta
desc: Alpharetta's walkable heart: 50+ shops and restaurants around Main Street, the Town Green with its splash fountain, City Hall, a self-guided arts walk of nearly 20 sculptures, and the Saturday farmers market in season.
tips: Use the parking decks at 92 Milton Avenue or 2 Park Plaza when street spots fill.
The Saturday farmers market runs April through mid-November on the Town Green.
Download the City Tours app to follow the arts and history walks.
about: Downtown Alpharetta centers on City Center and the Town Green next to City Hall, where a fountain gives kids a place to splash. Main Street, Canton Street and Milton Avenue hold the restaurants and independent shops, and small spots such as North Main Street Park with its gazebo and Milton Avenue Park with its log cabin add bits of history along the way.

Free self-guided tours make it easy to explore on foot. The Arts Walking Tour features nearly 20 sculptures, a mix of permanent and temporary pieces, and the History Walk links more than 25 historical markers. Behind City Hall, Brooke Street Park has a covered bandstand used for concerts.

Events fill the warmer months. The farmers market sets up on the Town Green on Saturday mornings from April to mid-November, and Food Truck Alley takes over Old Roswell Street on the fourth Thursday from April through October. Public parking decks sit at 92 Milton Avenue and 2 Park Plaza, and the Alpha Loop trail connects downtown to Avalon in about a mile.

name: Big Creek Greenway
desc: Alpharetta's signature trail: about 9 miles of wide paved path along Big Creek for walking, biking and skating, plus mountain-bike trails and a wetland boardwalk spur. Free, dawn to dusk, with access points at Rock Mill, Haynes Bridge, Northpoint and more.
tips: Start at Northpoint, Rock Mill or Preston Ridge Park if you want restrooms.
Beaver Creek Park is trail access only, with no parking.
The trail keeps going north into Forsyth County beyond McFarland Parkway.
about: The Big Creek Greenway is Alpharetta's main multi-use trail, a roughly 9-mile system of wide concrete path that follows Big Creek through wooded stream corridors. It is popular with walkers, runners, cyclists and families with strollers, and it continues north into Forsyth County, where a separate section begins at McFarland Parkway.

There are several places to start. Northpoint Park (6698 North Point Parkway), Rock Mill Park (3100 Kimball Bridge Road) and Preston Ridge Park (3657 Preston Ridge Road) have parking and restrooms. Haynes Bridge Park (10701 Haynes Bridge Road) and Marconi Park (900 Marconi Drive) have parking with portable restrooms, Union Hill Park off Little Pine Trail has parking, and Beaver Creek Park offers trail access only.
Because the path is paved and mostly gentle, it works well for an easy out-and-back of any length.

name: Ameris Bank Amphitheatre
desc: Alpharetta's 12,000-seat outdoor concert venue in a wooded setting at Encore Park, hosting major country, rock and pop tours from spring through fall.
tips: Plan to arrive about an hour early to beat traffic and security lines.
Coolers, picnic baskets and outside alcohol are not allowed; buy food inside.
Lawn tickets are general admission, so earlier arrival means a better spot.
about: Ameris Bank Amphitheatre is a 12,000-capacity outdoor concert venue on Encore Parkway, operated by Live Nation. It opened on May 10, 2008, with a performance by the Atlanta Symphony Orchestra, and carried the Verizon Wireless and later Verizon Amphitheatre names before Ameris Bank bought the naming rights in December 2018.

The schedule mixes touring pop, rock and country acts with comedians and themed symphony nights. Seating options include reserved seats in the orchestra and upper levels, plus general-admission lawn and pit areas for many shows.

Expect security screening at the gates, and leave coolers, picnic baskets and outside alcohol at home. Concession stands sell food and drinks, including picnic-style meals. On-site parking is spread across several lots that generally open about two hours before a show.

name: Wills Park
desc: Alpharetta's largest park at about 110 acres: sports fields, three playgrounds, a pool, disc golf, a community garden, loop trails and the Wills Park Equestrian Center.
about: Wills Park on Wills Road is Alpharetta's largest park and the city's main hub for recreation. Ball players use seven grass baseball fields, a synthetic turf field and two tee-ball fields, and there are six lighted tennis courts, batting cages, cornhole boards, outdoor fitness equipment and an 18-hole disc golf course spread across the grounds.

For families, there is the Wacky World Playground plus two more playgrounds, walking trails of 1.25 and 2 miles, an arboretum with about two dozen tree species, a community garden and two Little Free Libraries. The Alpharetta Community Center and Recreation Center provide gyms and indoor activity rooms.

Wills Park Pool, renovated in 2018, has a 10-lane competition pool with diving boards and a leisure pool with zero-depth entry, play features and a water slide. The park is also home to the Waggy World dog park, the Wills Park Equestrian Center and the historic Mansell House.
tips: Bring your own discs for the 18-hole disc golf course.
Three of the five picnic pavilions can be rented; the other two are first-come.
The pool entrance is at 1815 Old Milton Parkway.

name: Webb Bridge Park
desc: 109-acre park with sports fields, a lake, an arboretum and a crushed-limestone trail that loops about 1.7 miles along a creek.
about: Webb Bridge Park covers 109 acres off Kimball Bridge Road and mixes busy sports fields with quieter green space. It has three grass soccer fields, a synthetic turf multi-purpose field, four baseball fields and four tennis courts, along with concession stands for game days.

Away from the fields, a 1.5-mile walking trail, a lake and an arboretum with more than 20 tree specimens give the park a natural side. The arboretum represents upland hardwood forest, conifers and trees typical of moist ravines and bottomland.

Kids gravitate to the Webb Zone Playground, and there is outdoor fitness equipment, a Play Me Again piano and a Little Free Library. Dog owners can use the on-site dog park, which has separate areas for large and small dogs. Three picnic pavilions are available on a first-come, first-served basis.
tips: Picnic pavilions are first-come, first-served, so arrive early on weekends.
Use the separate small-dog area if your pup is shy around big dogs.
Walk the 1.5-mile trail past the lake and arboretum.

name: North Park
desc: 97-acre park with sports fields, a lake, a reflection garden, a 1-mile paved trail and the city's Adult Activity Center.
about: North Park is a 97-acre city park on Cogburn Road with a strong focus on sports. It has eight lighted softball fields, two synthetic turf multi-purpose fields, five lighted tennis courts and six pickleball courts, making it a regular stop for leagues and pickup games.

The park also has a quieter side. A walking trail circles past the lake, and the Rotary Reflection Garden offers a calm place to sit. Two playgrounds keep younger kids busy, and a Little Free Library is on site.

North Park is home to the city's Adult Activity Center and an Arts Building, so it draws visitors for classes as well as games. Two picnic pavilions are available, one first-come, first-served and one that can be rented for gatherings.
tips: Reserve the rentable pavilion ahead of a party.
Pickleball and tennis courts are lighted for evening play.
Visit the Rotary Reflection Garden for a quiet break.

name: Brooke Street Park
desc: 5-acre passive park behind City Hall with an arboretum, paved trail, stream, sculptures and a covered bandstand.
about: Brooke Street Park is a 5-acre passive park behind Alpharetta City Hall, along Haynes Bridge Road in downtown. A winding concrete path loops around an open lawn and a landscaped stream, making it an easy spot for a short walk.

The park doubles as an arboretum, with specimen trees and more than a dozen trees that flower in spring. Public art sculptures here are part of the Downtown Alpharetta Arts Walking Tour, and a covered bandstand on the lawn hosts local concerts and performances.

There are cornhole boards for casual play, and a small reflection garden sits between City Hall and the Fulton County Library. Restrooms are on the exterior ground floor of City Hall and in the parking garage across from the library, and free parking is available downtown. The park is open from dawn to dusk.
tips: Check the downtown events calendar for concerts at the bandstand.
Visit in spring when the flowering trees bloom.
Park in the free garage across from the library.

name: Rock Mill Park
desc: 20-acre park on Kimball Bridge Road with pavilions, an environmental education area and a popular Big Creek Greenway trailhead.
about: Rock Mill Park is a 20-acre city park on Kimball Bridge Road that serves as one of the main trailheads for the Big Creek Greenway. With on-site parking and restrooms, it is a practical place to start a walk, run or ride along the paved greenway.

The park is known for its green roof pavilion, and a smaller group pavilion is available first-come, first-served for family gatherings and celebrations. An outdoor classroom supports environmental education programs.

Because it is smaller and more natural than the city's sports parks, Rock Mill suits picnics and quiet time outdoors as much as greenway trips. From the trailhead you can head along Big Creek toward other access points such as Haynes Bridge Park or Northpoint Park.
tips: Use Rock Mill as a greenway starting point with parking and restrooms.
The small pavilion is first-come, first-served.
Look for the green roof on the main pavilion.

name: Union Hill Park
desc: City of Alpharetta park on 13 acres reached from Union Hill Road off Windward Parkway. It has an outdoor pop-up skate park, a covered roller hockey rink, a pavilion and concession stand available to rent, on-site parking and an access point for the Big Creek Greenway trail.
tips: Use the on-site parking as a starting point for the Big Creek Greenway.
Contact the city ahead of time to book the pavilion for a group event.
Call (678) 297-6130 to confirm amenities before planning around them.
about: Union Hill Park is a City of Alpharetta park at 1590 Little Pine Trail, reached from Union Hill Road off Windward Parkway near the Fulton and Forsyth county line. The city lists it as an access point for the Big Creek Greenway, with on-site parking.
The city describes a pop-up skate park, a covered roller hockey rink and a rentable pavilion and concession stand, though these details could not be confirmed from a current source.

name: Cogburn Road Park
desc: Nearly 6-acre neighborhood park with an arboretum, pavilions and a Play Me Again piano.
about: Cogburn Road Park is a six-acre neighborhood park in the Crabapple area, sized for an easy outing with young kids. Its large playground has separate sections for ages 2 to 5 and 5 to 12, and a 0.2-mile concrete path makes a short loop through the grounds.

The park doubles as one of Alpharetta's arboretums, with seven labeled trees meant as a small living museum for education and enjoyment. A Play Me Again piano, part of the city's public art program, invites anyone to sit down and play.
Two small pavilions are available on a first-come, first-served basis and work well for family picnics or a simple birthday gathering with a few friends.
tips: Arrive early to claim one of the two first-come pavilions.
The playground has separate areas for toddlers and older kids.
Try the Play Me Again piano while you are there.

name: Waggy World Paw Park
desc: 1.5-acre fenced, off-leash dog park for well-behaved pups.
about: Waggy World Paw Park is the off-leash dog park inside Wills Park, covering about 1.5 acres off Wills Road in downtown Alpharetta. It is divided into three fenced enclosures so dogs can play with others their size.

The large-dog area, for dogs over 25 pounds, is wooded with pine straw and has agility equipment and ramps. The small-dog area, for dogs under 25 pounds, has mature trees, grass and pine straw, and a third area is open to dogs of all sizes and is fully shaded. Benches are spread throughout, and waste stations are provided.
Water spigots and bowls are in the large- and small-dog areas, but not in the all-dogs area. The ground is mostly natural, so expect some mud after rain. Hours are 8am to sunset.
tips: Bring water if you plan to use the all-dogs area, which has no spigot.
Expect muddy paws after rain on the natural ground.
Use the small-dog side for pups under 25 pounds.

name: Alpha Loop
desc: A paved urban trail linking Downtown Alpharetta and Avalon, about a mile each way, with public art and pocket parks along the route.
about: The Alpha Loop is Alpharetta's growing network of urban multi-use trails, designed to link Downtown, Avalon, the North Point area and Northwinds. The paths are 12 feet wide and open to walkers, runners and cyclists.

The best-known segment connects Downtown Alpharetta and Avalon in about a mile, so it is easy to walk between dinner downtown and shopping at Avalon. Another section of roughly a mile, from Old Milton Parkway to Northwinds Parkway, opened on June 1, 2024. It passes through woods and along streams, ducks under Westside Parkway in a tunnel and includes an overlook bridge.
Permanent outdoor sculptures line both trails, adding public art to the route, and the loop continues to grow as the city builds new sections.
tips: Walk the Downtown-to-Avalon segment, about a mile each way.
Try the Old Milton to Northwinds section for a more wooded route.
Look for the outdoor sculptures placed along the trail.

name: Alpharetta Farm at Old Rucker Park
desc: A 2-acre working farm with gardens, a greenhouse and an outdoor classroom.
about: The Alpharetta Farm at Old Rucker Park, also called Old Rucker Farm, is a working organic vegetable farm on Rucker Road run by the city's Community Agriculture Program. Visitors can follow walking paths through the growing areas, and community garden plots let residents raise their own produce.

The farm is a hands-on learning spot. It offers volunteer opportunities, educational workshops and seasonal programs for all ages focused on sustainable growing, including summer Farm Fun sessions on topics such as bees, herbs and bird watching.
It is open to the public seven days a week from sunup to sundown, making it an easy, low-key stop for families who want kids to see where food comes from.
tips: Check the city's program listings for Farm Fun sessions and workshops.
Ask about volunteer days if you want to help in the fields.
Visit in daylight; the farm is open sunup to sundown.

name: Silos Park
desc: Small one-acre park in the Crabapple area built around four historic grain silos. Historical photos and a display explain how the silos once stored grain for local farms, making it a quick stop for a bit of local history while visiting Crabapple's shops and restaurants.
tips: Plan a short stop; the park is about one acre.
Read the historical photos to learn how the silos were used.
Pair it with a stroll through Crabapple's shops and restaurants.
about: Silos Park is a one-acre city park on Crabapple Road built around four historic grain silos. The silos once held grain for the area's farms, and historical photos on site show what Crabapple looked like during its farming days.

It is a small, quick stop rather than a full outing, and it fits naturally into a visit to the Crabapple area. Take a few minutes to read the displays and snap a photo of the silos, then continue on to the nearby shops and restaurants.
Families with history-curious kids may find it a simple way to talk about how the land around Alpharetta was used before the suburbs grew up around it.

name: Topgolf Alpharetta
desc: Point-scoring golf games for every skill level, with food and drinks served to your climate-controlled bay. Open year-round.
about: Topgolf Alpharetta on Westside Parkway is a three-level venue with more than 100 all-weather hitting bays, where microchipped balls score themselves as you aim at giant outfield targets.
