about: The Cole Team is a mother-daughter real estate team, Meriellen Cole and Stephanie Cole Patterson, now affiliated with REAL Broker and working from 44 Milton Avenue in downtown Alpharetta. The pair started in 2003 after moving to Forsyth County, famously marketing their first listings door to door in the Windermere neighborhood.

With more than 20 years in the business and over 1,000 homes sold, the team helps buyers and sellers in Alpharetta, Milton, Roswell, Cumming, Johns Creek and the Lake Lanier area. Stephanie brings an advertising background to how listings are marketed.
Sellers can request a free consultation to estimate a home's value before listing. The team is also known locally for its community involvement in north Fulton and Forsyth.

name: S&N Group - Keller Williams North Atlanta
desc: S&N Group is a Keller Williams North Atlanta team led by Surabhi and Nitin Arora that has helped more than 750 families buy, sell and invest in real estate. They serve Alpharetta, Johns Creek, Milton, Roswell, Cumming and Suwanee, with focus areas including first-time buyers, luxury homes, relocation and investors.
tips: Request a home valuation before listing
Set up listing alerts on the team's site while you search
Ask about relocation help if you are moving from out of state
about: S&N Group is a Keller Williams North Atlanta team led by Surabhi and Nitin Arora. The team reports helping more than 750 families buy, sell and invest, with more than $350 million in sales volume.

Its focus areas are Alpharetta, Johns Creek, Milton, Roswell, Cumming and Suwanee. The team works with first-time buyers, luxury buyers and sellers, families relocating to north Atlanta and real estate investors. Sellers get a marketing plan that can include professional photos, video, virtual tours and 3D walkthroughs.

The team's website includes property search with listing alerts, neighborhood reports, home value estimates and mortgage and affordability calculators, which are useful for early research before you talk to an agent.

name: The Kroupa Team - Berkshire Hathaway
desc: The Kroupa Team is led by Todd Kroupa of Berkshire Hathaway HomeServices Georgia Properties and has more than 20 years of experience selling luxury homes, residential property and equestrian estates. It serves Alpharetta, Milton, Roswell and North Metro Atlanta, with Todd acting as the single point of contact.
address: 33 S Main St, Ste 201, Alpharetta, GA 30009
tips: Ask about experience with farm and equestrian properties in Milton
Clients work directly with Todd rather than a rotating team
First responders and veterans should ask about his focus on their home searches
about: The Kroupa Team is led by Todd Kroupa, a Realtor and broker associate with Berkshire Hathaway HomeServices Georgia Properties, from an office at 33 South Main Street in downtown Alpharetta. Before real estate, he spent 23 years as a firefighter captain and paramedic, and he now has more than 20 years in the business.

He focuses on luxury homes, residential property and equestrian estates across Alpharetta, Milton, Roswell, Johns Creek, Canton and Cumming, and he has a particular interest in helping first responders and veterans buy homes. Atlanta Agent magazine reported he was the No. 1 individual agent for his brokerage in Georgia in 2024.
Kroupa is the team's only Realtor, so clients work with him directly, while his wife Abi leads marketing and a support staff handles administration.

name: The Cueny Team - Ansley Real Estate
desc: The Cueny Team works out of Ansley Real Estate Christie's International's North office on Church Street in downtown Alpharetta, helping clients buy, sell, relocate and invest in North Atlanta homes. Atlanta Agent magazine reported the team helped more than 141 families and sold over $133 million in homes in 2023.
tips: Schedule weekend showings directly with an agent
Ask about staging advice before you list
Ask about relocation and investment consulting
about: The Cueny Team works out of Ansley Real Estate Christie's International's North office at 31 Church Street in downtown Alpharetta, helping clients buy, sell, relocate and invest across north Atlanta. Andrea Cueny leads the team.

In 2024 the team helped more than 113 families and closed over $115 million in sales, ranking first in team sales volume and homes sold both at the North office and across Ansley Real Estate. Atlanta Agent magazine has also recognized it as a best team.

Seller services include home staging advice, negotiation and handling the transaction through closing. The office keeps weekday hours, so plan to set up evening or weekend showings directly with an agent.

name: Home with Sherry Team
desc: Home with Sherry Team is a Compass real estate team based at the Compass office on Northwinds Parkway, representing buyers and sellers across Alpharetta and North Atlanta. The team reported $65 million in sales volume in 2023, gets most of its business from referrals, and was named a 2023 Real Trends top 10 team in Georgia.
tips: Ask for a pre-listing assessment before you prepare your home
Browse current listings on the team's Compass page
Relocating buyers can ask for help comparing commutes and neighborhoods
about: Home with Sherry Team is a Compass real estate team based in Alpharetta, serving buyers and sellers from in-town Atlanta north to Lake Lanier. The team has more than 20 years in business and over 800 transactions.

It reported about $65 million in sales volume in 2023 and says more than 80 percent of its business comes from referrals. RealTrends named it a top 10 team in Georgia for 2023, and it has earned several Compass North Atlanta team awards.

For sellers, the team offers pricing strategy built on local data, a pre-listing home assessment, staging, trades referrals and management through closing. Buyers, including relocating families, get help weighing commute times, lot quality, amenities and planned development nearby. Current listings are posted on the team's Compass page.

name: Premier Atlanta Real Estate
desc: Premier Atlanta Real Estate is listed as a full-service agency in Alpharetta that represents buyers and sellers, analyzes investment properties and helps people relocating to the Atlanta area. We could not read its official website to confirm the office address or phone, so verify contact details before visiting.
tips: Confirm contact details before visiting
Ask about relocation help if you are moving to the area
Request an investment analysis if you are buying a rental
about: Premier Atlanta Real Estate is listed as a full-service real estate agency in Alpharetta. Directory information describes buyer and seller representation, investment property analysis and relocation help, with a service area that includes Alpharetta, Johns Creek, Roswell, Sandy Springs, Dunwoody and Marietta.
We could not confirm the office address, phone number or agents from the company's own website, so verify contact details before arranging a meeting.

name: Atlanta Fine Homes Sotheby's
desc: Atlanta Fine Homes Sotheby's International Realty is a luxury brokerage serving greater Atlanta, with agents covering Alpharetta, Milton and other north Fulton estate communities. It markets high-end homes through the Sotheby's International Realty global network. Contact the firm to reach its agents who work in Alpharetta.
tips: Ask for an agent who specializes in Alpharetta and Milton estates
Ask how listings are marketed through the Sotheby's global network
Contact the Sanctuary Parkway office for north Fulton listings
about: Atlanta Fine Homes Sotheby's International Realty is a luxury brokerage serving greater Atlanta, with an office in Suite 400 at 1125 Sanctuary Parkway in Alpharetta. Dozens of its agents work from that office and cover Alpharetta, Milton, Roswell and other north metro communities.

The firm markets higher-end homes, estate properties, and listings gain exposure through the Sotheby's International Realty global network. The Alpharetta office recorded around 150 sales over a recent twelve-month period.

Buyers and sellers can contact the firm to be matched with an agent who knows a specific neighborhood. Sellers should ask how the Sotheby's network and the firm's marketing will be used for their listing. Buyers can also browse the firm's current listings online before reaching out.

name: Dominique Dawes Gymnastics & Ninja Academy
desc: Gymnastics, ninja and tumbling academy from Olympic gold medalist Dominique Dawes that opened near North Point in 2026. Safety-focused coaches let each child progress at their own pace in a low-pressure setting, with programs for beginners through more advanced students in a modern facility.
tips: Flexible scheduling makes it easier to fit classes around school
Ninja classes suit kids who prefer obstacles over traditional gymnastics
Call to find the right level before enrolling
about: Dominique Dawes Gymnastics & Ninja Academy opened in 2026 at 380 North Point Circle, in the North Point area. It is run under the name of Olympic gold medalist Dominique Dawes and is part of her growing group of academies.

Programs cover gymnastics, ninja obstacle training and tumbling for children from beginners through more advanced students. Coaches emphasize safety and let each child progress at their own pace in a low-pressure, supportive setting. Ninja classes give kids who like obstacle courses an alternative to traditional gymnastics.
Families point to the clean, modern facility, convenient location and flexible class scheduling, which helps working parents fit classes around school and other activities.

name: Bach to Rock Alpharetta
desc: One-on-one lessons in piano, guitar, drums and voice, plus early-childhood music, camps and Battle of the Bands showcases, in Crabapple.
about: Bach to Rock Alpharetta is a music school in Suite 118 at 12315 Crabapple Road, locally owned by Carmen and Nancy Guinto. It serves families from Alpharetta, Milton, Roswell, Crabapple and nearby north Fulton and Cherokee communities.

Private lessons cover piano, guitar, bass, ukulele, drums, voice, brass, strings, woodwinds and songwriting, with beginner group classes and beat making as well. Early childhood programs start with toddlers, and students 7 and up can join a band or the Glee Club to play with peers at a similar level. Camps run during summer, spring and winter breaks and on school holidays, and the school hosts birthday parties.
Students perform at events such as Bachapalooza, smaller showcases and Battle of the Bands at a live music venue. The school is open seven days a week, with weekday hours until 8pm.
tips: Ask about joining a band once your child is 7 or older
Book school-holiday camps early
Weekday lessons run until 8pm for after-school schedules

name: The Metropolitan Club
desc: Upscale ballrooms and grounds on Windward Parkway for weddings, galas and corporate events, with on-staff coordinators.
about: The Metropolitan Club is an event venue at 5895 Windward Parkway that has hosted weddings and private events since 2003. It combines an indoor ballroom with landscaped lawns for open-air ceremonies and a covered outdoor space.

The venue can accommodate events of 300 or more guests, with separate ceremony and reception areas and a dressing room. Weddings, engagement parties, showers, rehearsal dinners, galas and corporate functions all take place here. Catering is handled in-house with buffet or family-style service, and the venue supplies tables, chairs, linens, a dance floor, bar service and service staff.

An on-staff planning team helps with decor, design, bar and menu choices and can recommend outside vendors such as photographers and transportation. There is ample parking on site, and multiple packages are offered for different budgets.
tips: Ask the planning team for outside vendor recommendations
Plan an outdoor lawn ceremony with the ballroom as a rain backup
Compare packages early to match your guest count

name: The Hotel at Avalon
desc: Avalon's flagship hotel, with ceremony and reception space steps from the district's shopping and dining.
about: The Hotel at Avalon, part of Marriott's Autograph Collection, anchors the Avalon district at 9000 Avalon Blvd. It opened with the adjoining Alpharetta Conference Center and has 330 guest rooms, with Avalon's shopping and dining just outside the door.

Event space totals about 35,000 square feet. The Teasley Ballroom can host a banquet-style wedding reception for up to 820 guests, and the Skelton Gallery adds another large space. Outdoor options include the pool terrace and cabanas, the East Lawn and an expansion terrace, which work well for ceremonies and cocktail hours.

Marriott-certified wedding planners help with budgets, menus, vendors and setup, and the hotel provides catering, audiovisual support and room blocks for out-of-town guests. South City Kitchen, the on-site restaurant, has private dining rooms for rehearsal dinners.
tips: Reserve a room block so out-of-town guests can walk to Avalon
Consider the East Lawn for an outdoor ceremony
Use South City Kitchen's private rooms for a rehearsal dinner

name: Three Birches Event Venue
desc: Three Birches Events Venue is a family-owned venue on a private, gated 6-acre estate that opened in 2017. It hosts weddings, corporate events and private parties in spaces that include the Grand Crystal Hall, a ceremony and lounge room, a romantic terrace and a lodge, with seating for up to about 150 guests.
tips: Bring your own caterer or use the venue's vendor list
Schedule a weekday or weekend tour through the online form
Plan for a guest count of 150 or fewer
about: Three Birches Event Venue occupies a private, gated and fenced 6-acre property at 200 Hickory Flat Road. The family-owned venue opened in 2017 and hosts weddings, corporate events and private parties.

Spaces include a ceremony hall, the Crystal Reception Hall, an outdoor pavilion and a cozy cabin house, along with a pool area, and the property has a farm setting. Events can seat up to about 150 guests. A dressing room, on-site accommodations and parking are available.

Couples can bring outside caterers and vendors or work from the venue's vendor list, and food and decor setup are arranged separately from the venue rental. Tours are offered on weekdays and weekends, and the venue's online form is the easiest way to request pricing and schedule a visit.

name: Reserve 116
desc: Reserve 116 is a modern industrial event space on Old Milton Parkway with white concrete walls and floors, an exposed white ceiling, barn doors and a statement fireplace. It hosts milestone celebrations, private dinners, corporate gatherings and brand activations, and includes a bar area, prep kitchen and Wi-Fi.
address: 4150 Old Milton Pkwy, Ste 116, Alpharetta, GA 30005
tips: Bring your own caterer, since there is no in-house food service
Plan seating for 50 or a standing event for up to 150
Review the cancellation terms before booking
about: Reserve 116 is a modern industrial event space in Suite 116 at 4150 Old Milton Parkway, in the Shops of Old Milton. The all-white room has concrete walls and floors, exposed beams, barn doors and a statement fireplace, with natural light throughout.

The open-plan space holds up to about 50 seated or 150 standing guests. It hosts milestone birthdays, bridal showers, private dinners, corporate gatherings, workshops and brand or product launches. A bar area, prep kitchen, Wi-Fi and a sound system with music speakers are included, and you can play your own music.

There is no in-house catering, so outside caterers are welcome, and guests may bring their own alcohol. Free on-site parking includes an accessible space. Bookings are made through the venue's inquiry form, and there is a minimum rental length.

name: Halcyon
desc: Forsyth County's answer to Avalon, a short drive up GA 400, with shops, restaurants and Big Creek Greenway access.
about: Halcyon is a 135-acre mixed-use district at 6365 Halcyon Way, just across the line in Forsyth County and a short drive north of Alpharetta along GA 400. It is often compared to Avalon, mixing shops, chef-driven restaurants, offices, a hotel and homes for sale or lease around a central green.
The Big Creek Greenway has a trailhead at Halcyon, so walkers, runners, cyclists and dog owners can start a trail outing and finish with dinner. Paved paths connect the shops and restaurants.

Hours vary by business, with most stores open from 10am into the evening Monday through Saturday and shorter hours on Sunday. It makes an easy evening out for Alpharetta families who want a change from downtown or Avalon.
tips: Start a Big Creek Greenway walk or bike ride from the Halcyon trailhead
Sunday store hours are shorter, so check before you go
Combine a trail outing with dinner on the green

name: Roswell Historic District
desc: Canton Street's restaurant row and the Southern Trilogy historic homes, 15 minutes south.
about: Roswell's historic district, about 15 minutes south of Alpharetta, covers roughly 120 acres around the town square and was listed on the National Register of Historic Places in 1974. Buildings date to as early as 1837, when the town grew up around the Roswell Manufacturing Company's cotton mill.

Visitors can tour the antebellum homes known as the Southern Trilogy. Bulloch Hall and Barrington Hall were both built in 1839, and the Smith Plantation completes the trio. The ruins of the original mill, burned by Union troops in 1864, sit in Old Mill Park, and the Old Bricks apartments once housed mill workers.
Nearby Canton Street is lined with restaurants, bars and boutiques in restored buildings, making it easy to pair a history walk with lunch or dinner.
tips: Pair a Southern Trilogy home tour with lunch on Canton Street
Walk the trails at Old Mill Park to see the mill ruins
Check tour days and times for the historic homes before you go

name: iFLY Indoor Skydiving
desc: Indoor skydiving in a vertical wind tunnel, about 30 minutes away near Cumberland.
about: iFLY Atlanta is an indoor skydiving center at 2778 Cobb Parkway SE, just off I-75 near Cumberland Mall and the Cobb Galleria Centre. It is about a 30-minute drive from Alpharetta.

Flyers float in a vertical wind tunnel that simulates the feeling of freefall. Every first-time flyer takes a short training session with a certified instructor, who then joins them in the flight chamber. Packages include flight time, training and gear rental, with larger goggles available for people who wear glasses.

Flyers must be at least 3 years old, and there is no upper age limit. Anyone under 18 needs a parent or guardian to sign the waiver. There is also a weight limit, so check the requirements before booking. Plan for about 90 minutes from check-in to finish.
tips: Arrive 20 minutes early to check in
Guests under 18 need a parent or guardian to sign the waiver
Plan about 90 minutes for the full visit

name: Foundation Social Eatery
desc: Husband-and-wife-run neighborhood restaurant known for house-made fettuccine and braised short rib hash.
about: Foundation Social Eatery is a neighborhood restaurant run by chef Mel Toledo and his wife, Sandy, at 55 Roswell Street in downtown Alpharetta. It first built a following in Roswell, closed there at the end of 2020, and reopened in Alpharetta in December 2022 in a more polished form.

The menu is French-inspired and changes with the seasons, while holding on to favorites such as house-made fettuccine, braised short rib hash and confit pork ribs. Caviar service and tableside sauce pours appear on the menu, and the bar program features classic cocktail riffs and French wines.

The space includes a main dining room, an open-air patio, a covered patio and a chef's table that looks into the kitchen. Dinner is served Monday through Saturday, and the restaurant is closed Sundays. Reservations are recommended, especially on weekends.
tips: Reserve ahead for weekend dinners
Request the chef's table for a view into the kitchen
Closed Sundays

name: Petite FSE
desc: Parisian-style cafe and market from the Foundation Social Eatery team, with paninis, baguettes and grab-and-go.
about: Petite FSE is the Parisian-inspired cafe and market inside Foundation Social Eatery at 55 Roswell Street, run by the same team. It opened in 2023 as a casual daytime counterpart to the main dining room.

The counter serves sandwiches such as a prosciutto melt with brie and arugula and a mushroom grilled cheese, plus salads including a Nicoise-style plate. A display case holds eclairs, cookies, scones and other pastries, and the market side sells house-made breads, pastas and sauces, olive oils and retail wine. Espresso drinks round out the menu.
Seating is communal, and much of the menu works as grab-and-go for a picnic or office lunch. The cafe has kept daytime hours rather than evening service, so check current hours before visiting.
tips: Pick up house-made pasta and sauce for dinner at home
Check hours before visiting, since the cafe keeps daytime hours
Grab pastries to go for a morning meeting

name: Flatlands Bourbon & Bayou
desc: Louisiana bayou flavors and a deep bourbon list in historic downtown.
about: Flatlands Bourbon & Bayou brings Louisiana and Creole cooking to a storefront at 52B North Main Street in historic downtown Alpharetta. The menu runs from starters and salads to po' boys and other sandwiches, with Creole plates such as shrimp and andouille and blackened redfish, plus fresh seafood and daily specials. A full bar backs up the bourbon in the name.

The restaurant is family owned. Jodi and Vinny Chieco, who also run Brick House Pizza and Pasta in Roswell, opened it in August 2016 with a grand opening celebration later that month. The dining room seats roughly 80, with a small bar and an outdoor patio for around 25 more, so it works for lunch, dinner or a relaxed date night.
tips: The patio is small, so arrive early if you want an outdoor table on a nice evening.
Ask about the daily specials, which change and often feature seafood.
Hours have been listed differently in different places, so call ahead to confirm before a late visit.

name: Chiringa
desc: Beach-shack-style spot with lobster rolls, tacos, bowls and one of downtown's most popular patios.
about: Chiringa is a casual, beach-bar-style restaurant in one of the two small jewel box buildings on the Alpharetta City Center Town Green, at 34 South Main Street. The name is Spanish for kite, and the concept takes its cue from a beach bar in Spain, with a sister restaurant called Chiringo on the 30A coast of Florida.

Ordering is at the counter. The kitchen focuses on seafood and organic or grass-fed meats, with Baja tacos made with white fish, chicken or Gulf shrimp, a fish sandwich on brioche and a cheeseburger, along with chips and salsa. Cocktails are mixed with juice squeezed in house.
Seating for about 100 includes a patio that spills toward the Town Green along Main Street, which makes it a natural stop before or after an event on the green. Owner Andy McKoski opened it in 2018.
tips: Grab a patio seat facing the Town Green for people watching on weekend evenings.
Order at the counter, then find a table, since service is counter style.
Check the city events calendar, since the Town Green gets busy during concerts and festivals.

name: Truck & Tap
desc: Rotating food trucks paired with a curated craft beer list on Milton Avenue.
about: Truck & Tap on Milton Avenue pairs a rotating lineup of food trucks with a bar pouring craft beer, so the food changes depending on which truck is parked out front that day. Past trucks have included pizza, Caribbean and comfort food vendors. The bar opened with 12 craft beers on tap and also serves wine, cocktails, craft sodas and nitro cold brew.

The downtown Alpharetta spot opened in November 2017 as a mostly outdoor venue, and it is a sister to the Truck & Tap in Woodstock. Expect a casual setup where you order food from the truck and drinks from the bar, then settle in at the outdoor tables.
Events such as trivia nights, tap takeovers and cornhole are part of the routine, which makes it a relaxed option for groups and after-work meetups a short walk from the City Center.
tips: Check the social media schedule to see which food truck is on site before you go.
Bring a jacket on cooler evenings, since much of the seating is outdoors.
Look for trivia nights and tap takeovers if you want a livelier crowd.

name: Lapeer Steak & Seafood
desc: Chef-inspired steak and seafood with rotating oysters and a large reserve wine list.
about: Lapeer Steak & Seafood sits at 12 North Broad Street in Alpharetta City Center. It opened in 2019 as Lapeer Seafood Market and was reworked into a steakhouse in February 2022. It is part of Maven Restaurant Group, the team behind South Main Kitchen and Butcher & Brew, with Louis Soon as owner.

Expect a menu that pairs classic steakhouse dishes, such as beef tartare, French onion soup, a center-cut filet and a Prime Delmonico ribeye, with seafood carried over from the original concept, including smoked fish dip, lobster pasta and a warm lobster roll. Oysters rotate, and the bar focuses on classic cocktails and a reserve wine list.

The roughly 3,000 square foot room has 15-foot ceilings, an open kitchen and an enclosed, climate-controlled patio overlooking City Center. Dinner is the focus, and reservations are taken through OpenTable.
tips: Book through OpenTable for weekend dinners, since it is a popular special-occasion spot.
Ask for the enclosed patio if you want a view of City Center.
Sundays are closed, so plan a weeknight or Saturday visit.

name: Minnie Olivia Pizzeria
desc: Neo-Neapolitan wood-fired pies just off the Town Green.
about: Minnie Olivia Pizzeria serves wood-fired pizzas, pastas and Italian small plates from the historic Dodd Hotel building at 10 Roswell Street, steps from the Town Green. The restaurant takes its name from Minnie Olivia Dodd, for whom the building is named, and it has a full bar.

Chef Julio Delgado, formerly executive chef at New Realm Brewing and JP Atlanta, opened it in November 2019. The space is intimate, with about 38 seats inside including a small bar, and roughly 40 more on the outdoor patio.
It suits a casual dinner downtown, a lunch break or a pizza before an evening on the green. Pizzas come out of a wood-fired oven, and the full bar pours cocktails, beer and wine to go with them.
tips: The indoor dining room is small, so the patio is your best bet for groups on nice days.
Come early on weekend evenings, when downtown restaurants fill quickly.
Pair a pizza with one of the Italian small plates to share.

name: Taffer's Tavern
desc: Jon Taffer's neighborhood-pub concept with burgers, flatbreads and cocktails.
about: Taffer's Tavern is a casual dining tavern created by Jon Taffer of the TV series Bar Rescue, and the downtown Alpharetta location at 33 South Main Street was the first in the brand's national rollout when it opened in October 2020.

The menu covers pub and comfort plates such as burgers, braised short ribs, fish and chips and glazed salmon, alongside cocktails developed by the show's mixologist Phil Wills and draft beers poured using Taffer's own method. The kitchen is fully electric and relies on sous vide cooking.

Inside, look for a chandelier made from bourbon bottles at the entrance, brick pillars, oak counters and a large painting of Taffer above the fireplace. Big booths in the back work well for groups, and late hours on weekends make it an option after other downtown kitchens close.
tips: Reserve through OpenTable for larger groups who want one of the back booths.
It stays open late on Fridays and Saturdays, handy after a downtown event.
Try one of the signature cocktails from the Bar Rescue mixologist.

name: Curry Up Now
desc: Fast-casual Indian street food on South Main.
about: Curry Up Now is a fast-casual Indian street food chain from the San Francisco area, and its Alpharetta store faces the Town Green on South Main Street in Alpharetta City Center. The menu reworks Indian flavors into bowls, burritos and sandwiches built with curries, ghee and paneer.

The roughly 1,800 square foot restaurant opened in spring 2021 under owner Hemant Suri, a longtime Alpharetta resident who operates other Curry Up Now stores in metro Atlanta. Ordering is quick and casual, which makes it a practical lunch stop or a takeout dinner downtown.
It is a good choice for groups with mixed tastes, since vegetarian proteins like paneer sit alongside meat options.
tips: Order ahead online for a quick pickup at lunch.
Vegetarian diners will find paneer-based options across bowls and burritos.
Eat outside on the Town Green when the weather is nice.

name: Beignets & Brew
desc: Fresh beignets and locally roasted coffee all day on South Main.
about: Beignets & Brew is a cafe at 230 South Main Street in downtown Alpharetta built around freshly fried beignets and locally roasted coffee, both served all day. It is part of a regional cafe brand with locations across Georgia, Alabama, Florida, Tennessee and Arkansas.
Expect a casual coffee shop setting that works for a morning coffee run, an afternoon treat or a sweet stop after dinner downtown. Online ordering is available through Toast for pickup.
tips: Beignets are best eaten warm, so enjoy them on site if you can.
Online ordering is available for a quick pickup.
Call ahead to confirm current hours.

name: Jinya Ramen Bar
desc: Rich tonkotsu ramen with vegan options on South Broad.
about: JINYA Ramen Bar is a Los Angeles-born ramen chain, and its Alpharetta restaurant sits at 401 South Broad Street in the City Center area. Opened in 2019 by a local franchise team, it was one of the larger JINYA locations in metro Atlanta, with a separate bar and dining room.

Pork-broth tonkotsu bowls are the core of the menu, including the Tonkotsu Original, Tonkotsu Black and a Premium Tonkotsu Red with adjustable spice levels. Chicken-broth bowls, a birria ramen and a tan tan men round it out. Plant-based diners have the Spicy Creamy V and the Flying V Harvest, plus Impossible gyoza, tacos and buns.
Small plates such as crispy chicken, takoyaki, Brussels sprouts tempura and pork gyoza pair with Japanese beers, sake and cocktails, and there is a happy hour menu.
tips: Ask staff which bowls are fully vegan, since the menu labels them as vegetarian or plant based.
Look for the happy hour menu for discounted small plates and drinks.
Order a side of crispy chicken or gyoza to share while you wait for the ramen.

name: Kale Me Crazy
desc: Fresh organic juices, bowls and natural foods on Canton Street.
about: Kale Me Crazy is a superfood cafe at 50 Canton Street, Suite 101, in downtown Alpharetta. It is part of a metro Atlanta-founded chain started by Roi Shlomo, whose own change in eating habits in 2012 inspired the concept.

The menu centers on cold-pressed juices, smoothies made with plant-based milk, acai bowls, wraps, salads and avocado toast, with plenty of vegan and gluten-free options. Expect a casual counter-service cafe with outdoor seating, suited to breakfast, a quick lunch or a post-workout snack.
tips: Try an acai bowl or vegan wrap, two of the most mentioned items.
Ask about gluten-free options if you need them.
Call ahead to confirm current hours.

name: Siena
desc: Mediterranean-Italian newcomer (opened 2026) with seafood, house-made pasta and cocktails on Devore Road.
about: Siena is a Mediterranean and Italian restaurant at 124 Devore Road, named for the Tuscan city and built around the idea of coastal Mediterranean dining and gathering around the table. It opened in December 2025 with a women-led team: co-owner Aida Lemma runs day-to-day operations, with executive chef Baba Estavillo in the kitchen.

The menu is designed for sharing, tapas style. Expect plates such as whipped feta with burnt honey, crispy halloumi with grilled grapes, shrimp Francese arancini, octopus al ajillo, golden oxtail and Moroccan-style chicken, with desserts like saffron creme brulee and baklava cheesecake. A full bar serves cocktails.
The bar glows with green lighting, a second dining room opens up as a patio in warm weather, and a saxophonist plays on Friday nights. There is a free parking lot, and the restaurant is dine-in only.
tips: Reserve on OpenTable, especially for Friday nights when there is live saxophone.
Order several small plates to share rather than one entree each.
It is dine-in only, so do not plan on takeout.

name: Little Alley Steak
desc: Upscale steakhouse that opened on South Main in 2026, from the longtime Roswell favorite.
about: Little Alley Steak's Alpharetta location occupies the former Salt Factory Pub space at 102 South Main Street, which closed in July 2025 after 15 years. It is the third location for the steakhouse, following the Roswell original and a larger Buckhead restaurant, and it comes from the same restaurant group that ran Salt Factory.

The menu centers on wet-aged and dry-aged steaks, with oysters, shellfish and other seafood, backed by a wine and spirits program. It is an upscale, special-occasion kind of steakhouse, and tables can be booked through OpenTable.

Dinner runs every evening, with later closing on Fridays and Saturdays, and a Sunday lunch service has been listed as well. The downtown address puts it within walking distance of Alpharetta City Center and the Town Green.
tips: Book a table on OpenTable for weekend dinners.
Ask about the dry-aged cuts, a focus of the menu.
Park in the downtown city decks and walk over, since Main Street parking fills up.

name: Kona Grill
desc: Scratch-kitchen American menu plus sushi at Avalon.
about: Kona Grill at Avalon combines a contemporary American menu with sushi, steaks and seafood, served in a lively room with an indoor fireplace, big windows and an indoor-outdoor bar. It sits at 5100 Avalon Boulevard near Old Milton Parkway, close to the Regal cinema, and opened as part of the national chain's expansion in 2014.
Popular orders include salmon, steak frites and sushi and salad combinations, and diners often mention the jalapeno yellowtail sashimi. Specialty cocktails and margaritas are a big part of the draw.

The restaurant runs a happy hour and late-night happy hour with discounted bites and drinks, a weekday lunch menu and a Sunday brunch. There is patio seating in addition to the dining room, and reservations are available on OpenTable.
tips: Visit during happy hour or late-night happy hour for discounted sushi and drinks.
Sunday brunch starts at 10am.
Park in the Avalon decks and walk over if you are catching a movie at the nearby Regal.

name: NFA Burger
desc: Second location of the cult-favorite burger spot that began as a pop-up and then a gas station counter, opened at Avalon in 2025. The signature is a double-stacked smashed cheeseburger, served with tots or fries, hot dogs and milkshakes, in a full-service room with a bar.
tips: Expect a line at peak weekend lunch and dinner, since there are no reservations.
Order a side of tots, a house favorite.
Park free in the Avalon decks.
about: NFA Burger, short for Not Fooling Around, is Billy Kramer's burger brand that first drew a following from a counter inside a Dunwoody Chevron station. The Avalon restaurant at 3180 Avalon Boulevard opened in May 2025 in a space roughly ten times the size of the original.

The draw is the smashed burger, with Billy's Classic stacking two patties, American cheese, pickles, mustard and house Sassy Sauce, and options for more patties and toppings such as hatch green chiles or bacon. There are also hot dogs, fries and tots fried in beef tallow, a kids menu and frozen custard milkshakes, floats and sundaes, plus Liege waffles.

You order at the counter and staff bring food to your table inside or on the outdoor seating facing the courtyard by the Regal theater. A full bar serves drinks, and Avalon's decks offer free parking. There are no reservations.

name: Eddie V's Prime Seafood
desc: Upscale prime seafood and steak house that opened on Haynes Bridge in late 2025.
about: Eddie V's Prime Seafood is Darden's upscale seafood and steak brand, and its Alpharetta restaurant at 11405 Haynes Bridge Road was the first in Georgia. It opened in October 2025 in a custom 11,650 square foot building that replaced the former Sage Woodfire Tavern.
Seafood is the focus, with steaks, salads and sides filling out the menu. Shareable sides include truffled macaroni and cheese, and the menu offers premium touches like caviar.

Expect a polished, dressy dinner setting suited to anniversaries, business dinners and celebrations, with a full bar and wine list. The restaurant is near the Haynes Bridge Road exit off GA 400. Reservations are recommended, particularly on weekends, when the dining room is busiest.
tips: Make a reservation, particularly for weekend evenings.
Dress up a bit, since the setting leans upscale.
It sits near GA 400 at Haynes Bridge Road, which makes it easy to reach from either direction.

name: Sid's
desc: Surf-shack-themed 1970s-style pizza joint with music and a backyard on Haynes Bridge.
about: Sid's Pizza is a family-run pizza joint from husband and wife Stan and Sharon Kurnett, whose original restaurant in Suwanee has a surfer vibe that nods to Stan's Southern California roots. The Alpharetta location at 11770 Haynes Bridge Road, Suite 301, in the Alpharetta Crossing shopping center, is their second, set in the former Mellow Mushroom space with a 1970s basement feel.

Sicilian-style pizza leads the menu, alongside bowls, sandwiches, burgers, salads and wings. It is a relaxed, family-friendly spot for a casual dinner or a game night with friends, and catering is available for events.
The brand marked 20 years in business and has begun franchising. Takeout and delivery are available for nights at home.
tips: Try the Sicilian-style pizza, the house specialty.
Order catering for parties and office events.
Parking is easy in the Alpharetta Crossing shopping center lot.

name: Shake Shack
desc: Roadside-style Angus burgers, crinkle fries and shakes on Haynes Bridge.
about: This Shake Shack at 11780 Haynes Bridge Road opened in February 2022 as the fifth location in metro Atlanta, and it was built with a Shack Track drive-up window. Guests order ahead on the Shack app or website and collect food without leaving the car.

The menu covers the chain's roadside-style classics: the ShackBurger made with Angus beef, the Chicken Shack, crinkle-cut fries, hot dogs and hand-spun shakes and frozen custard, plus rotating seasonal items and lemonades.

Inside, ordering is by kiosk, and there is both an indoor dining room and a patio. Delivery and pickup orders also run through the app, which makes it a convenient stop for families and commuters near GA 400.
tips: Order in the app and use the drive-up window to skip the line.
Grab a patio table on mild days.
Check the app for seasonal shakes and limited-time items.

name: Original ChopShop
desc: Health-focused salads, bowls, wraps and protein shakes on Haynes Bridge.
about: Original ChopShop is a better-for-you counter-service restaurant, and its Alpharetta store at 10920 Haynes Bridge Road opened on October 9, 2024. It was the company's third Georgia location and 26th overall.

The kitchen uses whole ingredients across breakfast, lunch, snacks and dinner, so you can stop in for an acai bowl in the morning or a bowl or salad later in the day. Menu picks named by the company include the teriyaki chicken bowl, the Citrus Thai Chop salad and the acai bowl, and the lineup also includes wraps, sandwiches and protein shakes.
You can dine in, take food to go or order through the app and website, and catering is available for offices and events. The Chops loyalty program rewards repeat visits.
tips: Join the Chops loyalty program in the app to earn rewards.
Order ahead online for a fast pickup at lunch.
It opens at 9am, so it works for a breakfast acai bowl.

name: Connors Steak & Seafood
desc: Mesquite-grilled prime beef, fresh seafood, a raw bar and a big bourbon list on Windward Parkway.
about: Connors Steak & Seafood at 5045 Windward Parkway is part of Connor Concepts, a restaurant company established in 1992. The menu pairs prime and choice steaks and chops with mesquite-grilled entrees and fresh seafood, along with a raw oyster bar.

Diners often mention the tuna stack, the chilled seafood tower and the spinach and strawberry salad. The full bar has an extensive wine list, local beers and a large bourbon and whiskey selection, and happy hour runs daily from 3 to 6:30pm in the bar and lounge.
Lunch is served daily until 4pm before the dinner menu takes over, and reservations are available through OpenTable. The restaurant tends to fill up, so booking ahead is a good idea.
tips: Reserve on OpenTable, since tables fill up at dinner.
Stop by for daily happy hour from 3 to 6:30pm in the bar.
Lunch is served daily until 4pm.

name: Harth
desc: All-day restaurant inside the Hilton Alpharetta on Windward Parkway.
about: Harth is the restaurant and bar inside the Hilton Alpharetta Atlanta at 5775 Windward Parkway. It describes its cooking as elevated Southern cuisine with global influences, using seasonal ingredients from a scratch kitchen, under executive chef Bruno Vergara.

Breakfast runs daily from 7am to 2pm, with dishes such as avocado toast, huevos rancheros and steak and eggs, and dinner runs from 5 to 10pm. Shareable flatbreads and updated comfort dishes are part of the menu, and shrimp and grits is a signature.

The modern dining room is joined by an open-air terrace with fireplaces and a fire pit, and the lounge serves cocktails and wine. Dress is casual, it is open to locals as well as hotel guests, and parking is in the hotel lot.
tips: Book a terrace table by the fireplaces on cool evenings.
Try the shrimp and grits, a house signature.
Reservations are available through OpenTable and the restaurant's site.

name: Java Saga
desc: Alpharetta outpost of Doraville's Java Saga, opened in 2026 just off Windward Parkway with indoor seating. The menu centers on Taiwanese fried chicken sandwiches and cutlets, coffee and tea drinks and all-day breakfast items such as Taiwanese crepes, with the ABC sandwich as a standout.
address: 2905 Jordan Ct, Ste H, Alpharetta, GA 30022
tips: Go early, since the fried chicken can sell out before the afternoon.
Try the ABC sandwich, the dish the brand is known for.
Unlike the Doraville shop, there is indoor seating here.
about: Java Saga began as a coffee food truck in Doraville and built its reputation on Taiwanese fried chicken before opening a takeaway shop on Buford Highway. Owner Alvin Sun brought the brand to Alpharetta in 2026 with a roughly 1,600 square foot cafe at 2905 Jordan Court, Suite H, just off Windward Parkway.

The menu covers Taiwanese fried chicken sandwiches and cutlets with house sauces, coffee and tea drinks and all-day breakfast items such as Taiwanese crepes. The ABC sandwich is the order most people associate with the original location.
Unlike the Doraville takeaway counter, the Alpharetta cafe has indoor seating, so you can sit down with a sandwich and a drink rather than grabbing it to go.

name: Fiorenza
desc: Family-run Tuscan restaurant that opened in 2026 on Webb Bridge Way.
about: Fiorenza Italian is a family-run Tuscan restaurant at 11500 Webb Bridge Way, opened in late June 2026 by Alpharetta couple Jessi and Brooke Qilafi. Jessi grew up in Florence and has worked in restaurants in Italy, New York City and metro Atlanta for more than 15 years.

The menu follows a traditional Italian structure of antipasti, primi, secondi, contorni and dolci, with pasta made by hand. Executive chef Eugene Thompson, whose resume includes Oak Steakhouse and Davio's, leads the kitchen, and the bar pours Italian wines and craft cocktails.
The owners aim for a neighborhood feel with a lively, contemporary room, suited to family dinners and date nights. Reservations are taken through OpenTable or by phone, and walk-ins are welcome.
tips: Reserve on OpenTable or call (470) 359-6558 for weekend dinners.
Order a handmade pasta as your primi course.
It is closed Mondays.

name: Creation Social House
desc: Mediterranean restaurant and bar on Webb Bridge Way.
address: 11500 Webb Bridge Way Ste A7, Alpharetta, GA 30005
about: Creation Social House is a family-owned Mediterranean restaurant and bar at 11500 Webb Bridge Way, Suite A7. The kitchen leans Turkish, with lamb and chicken Adana kebabs, steak kebab, lahmacun, lamb chops, falafel, baba ghanoush and grilled wings, and the bar is known for craft cocktails, including a smoky Old Fashioned.
Entertainment is a big part of the experience. The weekly lineup has included live music, Thursday karaoke and weekend DJ nights, along with occasional international theme nights and concerts.

The space has a main bar, a second room with its own bar and a private dining area for large parties, so it is often booked for celebrations. Brunch has been offered on weekend mornings, and dress is casual.
tips: Check the weekly entertainment schedule before you go if you want karaoke or a DJ night.
Ask about the private dining room for birthday parties and group events.
Call the restaurant directly for reservations.

name: Koi Kaiten Sushi
desc: Revolving conveyor-belt sushi bar on Old Milton Parkway.
about: Koi Kaiten Sushi is a Japanese restaurant at 4180 Old Milton Parkway, Suite 1I, built around a revolving conveyor-belt sushi bar. Diners can pull plates of sushi straight off the belt as they pass or order from the menu.
The format suits a quick, casual meal and is fun for kids and groups who like to sample a variety of rolls and small plates. Takeout and delivery are also available through delivery apps.
tips: Sit at the belt to grab plates as they go by.
Order from the menu if you do not see what you want on the belt.
Call ahead to confirm current hours.

name: Ramen Bar by Hajime
desc: Casual ramen shop on Old Milton Parkway serving rich tonkotsu, shoyu miso and spicy bowls, plus buns, dumplings and curry. Vegetarian options include a spicy kale ramen and a shoyu miso version, and the team behind it also runs Kin No Tori Ramen Bar.
address: 4180 Old Milton Pkwy, Unit 1, Alpharetta, GA 30005
tips: Plan an early dinner, since it closes at 8pm.
Ask staff to confirm ingredients if you need a strictly vegan bowl.
Add a side of buns or dumplings to share.
about: Ramen Bar by Hajime is a casual ramen shop at 4180 Old Milton Parkway, Unit 1, from the same team that later opened Kin No Tori Ramen Bar. Service is quick and the setting relaxed, which makes it an easy weeknight dinner or lunch stop.

Bowls include rich tonkotsu, shoyu miso and spicy ramen, and the menu adds steamed buns, dumplings and curry. Vegetarian diners can choose the shoyu miso ramen or a spicy kale ramen, with tofu and shiitake mushrooms as proteins.
The restaurant serves lunch and dinner seven days a week but closes at 8pm, earlier than many restaurants nearby. Takeout is a popular option for nearby offices and families.

name: Smallcakes
desc: Cupcakes baked fresh daily on Old Milton Parkway.
about: Smallcakes is a cupcake shop at 4055 Old Milton Parkway, part of a national cupcakery franchise. The shop has offered around 15 signature flavors baked fresh each morning, along with rotating daily specials that change through the month.
It suits a quick dessert stop, a birthday treat or an order for an event, and the shop has offered delivery for parties and gifts.
tips: Ask about the daily rotating flavor.
Order ahead for parties and events.
Call ahead to confirm current hours.

name: Clean Juice
desc: USDA-certified organic juice bar on Old Milton Parkway serving organic juices and smoothies along with healthy, satisfying snacks. It is one of the Atlanta-area Clean Juice locations still operating after several metro stores closed in 2026, and it opens early for a breakfast stop.
tips: It opens at 7am on weekdays, handy for a pre-work smoothie.
Order ahead for a quick pickup during the lunch rush.
Ask about juice cleanse programs if you want a multi-day plan.
about: Clean Juice is part of a national organic juice bar franchise, and its Alpharetta store sits at 2500 Old Milton Parkway. The menu centers on organic cold-pressed juices such as Green Glow and blended smoothies, with seasonal flavors, cold brew and juice cleanse programs.

Food runs to quick, wholesome snacks, including toasts like peanut butter with banana and hemp seed. It is a counter-service stop that works for a morning smoothie on the way to work, a post-workout drink or a light lunch.
The store opens at 7am on weekdays and a little later on weekends, which makes it one of the earlier healthy options along this stretch of Old Milton Parkway.

name: Cork & Kale
desc: Health-forward market and bar inside the EVEN Hotel near Avalon on Old Milton Parkway, serving lighter, wellness-minded food alongside drinks. It works as a grab-and-go stop for hotel guests and locals and as a casual spot for a glass of wine or a healthy bite before or after visiting Avalon.
tips: Stop in for breakfast if you are staying at or near the EVEN Hotel.
The 24-hour market is handy for grab-and-go snacks.
Avalon is across the street, so it pairs well with a shopping trip.
about: Cork & Kale is the onsite fast-casual restaurant at the EVEN Hotel Alpharetta, on Old Milton Parkway across from Avalon. The hotel opened in early 2020 as the wellness-focused EVEN brand's first Georgia location.

The menu balances lighter, health-minded dishes with more indulgent choices, with examples such as an egg white and avocado wrap, a Beyond burger and a protein chicken bowl. It serves breakfast and dinner daily, and the hotel also has a full bar for beer, wine and cocktails plus a 24-hour market with prepared foods, snacks and drinks.
It is a practical option for hotel guests and for locals looking for a quick, healthy bite before or after a trip to Avalon.

name: Flavor Juicery
desc: Cold-pressed juice, vegan bowls and smoothies on Kimball Bridge.
about: Flavor Juicery opened its first storefront in 2016 at 4620 Kimball Bridge Road, Suite 2, and later added a Johns Creek location. Owner Uday Patel has said the business grew out of a personal mission to overcome illness, starting as a small operation selling just five juices.

Today the quick-service menu covers organic and cold-pressed juices, fruit smoothies, protein shakes and vegan bowls, along with acai bowls, sandwiches and salads. Ingredients are often sourced locally.

It works as a fast breakfast, a post-workout stop or a healthy lunch to go, and online ordering is available through Toast. The shop sits on Kimball Bridge Road, a short drive from the Old Milton Parkway corridor, with parking in the shopping center lot.
tips: Order ahead online through Toast for quick pickup.
Try an acai bowl or a cold-pressed juice.
Ask about vegan bowls if you eat plant based.

name: Kokee Tea
desc: Freshly brewed boba tea near North Point.
about: Kokee Tea is a bubble tea shop at 2176 North Point Circle, in the North Point shopping district beside North Point Mall. It is part of a small regional boba brand with a second Alpharetta store at Alpharetta Commons on Old Milton Parkway.

The menu covers freshly brewed milk teas, fruit teas and brown sugar boba, with oat and coconut milk available. Expect a small counter-service cafe with a few tables, walk-in service and free parking.
tips: Ask for oat or coconut milk if you avoid dairy.
Parking is free in the shopping center lot.
Call ahead to confirm current hours.

name: One Zo
desc: Taiwanese boba brand that makes its tapioca pearls in-store, on North Main.
about: One Zo is a Taiwanese bubble tea brand founded in 2015 that is known for making its tapioca pearls in store rather than using pre-made boba. This listing places the shop at 875 North Main Street in Alpharetta.

Menus at One Zo shops typically feature milk teas, fruit teas and brown sugar drinks such as a brown sugar dirty oolong latte, with fresh boba prepared on site. Expect a counter-service shop suited to a quick drink or an afternoon treat.
tips: Ask what pearl flavors were made that day.
Try a brown sugar drink to taste the fresh boba.
Call ahead to confirm the location and hours.

name: Dos Margaritas
desc: Casual, family-friendly Mexican restaurant in Crabapple known for scratch-made dishes and handcrafted margaritas. Popular orders include street tacos, fajitas, carne asada, shrimp bowls and chimichangas, with vegetarian-friendly options, outdoor patio seating, takeout and delivery.
tips: Grab a patio table on nice evenings.
Order family fajitas for a group of two to four.
Join the online ordering loyalty program to earn points on takeout.
about: Dos Margaritas is a casual, family-friendly Mexican restaurant at 12460 Crabapple Road, Suite 601, in the Crabapple area of Alpharetta. The menu is broad, covering dips, soups and salads, quesadillas, nachos, enchiladas, burritos, tacos and combination plates, plus steak, chicken and seafood specialties.

Fajitas are a mainstay, including traditional, tropical and family-size versions meant for two to four people, and the shrimp bowl and enchiladas suizas are regular orders. There is a dedicated vegetarian section and a kids menu, and the bar is known for margaritas and seasonal cocktails.
Outdoor patio seating is available, and takeout and delivery are offered for nights at home. Online orders through Toast earn loyalty points.

name: Aunty's Kitchen
desc: South Indian dosas and chaats on North Main.
about: Aunty's Kitchen is a vegetarian South Indian restaurant at 735 North Main Street, Suite 700. The menu focuses on dosas, chaats and street snacks such as panipuri, with several vegan options marked on the menu.

Expect a casual setting with outdoor seating. It has kept limited, mostly evening hours, with the restaurant closed early in the week, so check before you go. Portions are modest, which makes it easy to order several dishes to share.
tips: Order a few dishes to share, since portions are on the smaller side.
Check hours before going, since it has been closed Monday through Wednesday.
Ask staff to point out the vegan items.

name: Godavari
desc: South Indian restaurant from the national Godavari chain at Windward Promenade on North Main Street. The menu leans on Andhra and Hyderabadi cooking, including biryanis, dosas and Indo-Chinese dishes, with regional specialties such as chicken liver fry and fish pollichathu.
address: 865 N Main St, Ste 108, Alpharetta, GA 30004
tips: Try a regional specialty like fish pollichathu alongside a biryani.
Ask about catering for large family events.
Call ahead to confirm current hours before visiting.
about: Godavari is part of a national chain of South Indian restaurants, and its Alpharetta location occupies a corner unit, Suite 108, at Windward Promenade on North Main Street. It was the chain's first metro Atlanta restaurant when it signed its lease in 2017, in a space of about 5,100 square feet.

The kitchen draws on Andhra and Hyderabadi cooking, with Hyderabadi biryani, many kinds of dosa and Indo-Chinese dishes. Regional specialties such as chicken liver fry and fish pollichathu help set it apart from more general Indian menus.

The roomy dining room works for families and groups, and the restaurant also offers catering for parties and events. Windward Promenade has its own parking lot, and the restaurant sits on the busy North Main Street corridor near Windward Parkway.

name: Amma Kitchen
desc: Modern Indian kitchen on Cumming Street.
about: Amma Kitchen is a small, vegetarian South Indian restaurant at 390 Cumming Street, Suite A, connected to a small temple. It is known for a homemade feel and a modern take on classic dishes, including dosas, thalis and snacks such as poori bhaji, upma and chana bhatura.
It has served lunch and dinner on weekdays and Saturdays, with takeout available through delivery apps.
tips: Go at lunch for a thali.
Order takeout through delivery apps if you are short on time.
Call ahead to confirm hours, since it has been closed on Sundays.

name: Kakatiya Indian Kitchen
desc: Takeout-popular Telugu-style Indian kitchen near Windward.
address: 2905 Jordan Ct Ste A, Alpharetta, GA 30004
about: Kakatiya Indian Kitchen is a South Indian restaurant at 2905 Jordan Court, Suite A, near Windward Parkway. It is popular for takeout, though the simple dining room with small Indian touches also works for a sit-down meal.
The menu covers biryani, curries, fresh naan, street food such as samosa chaat, and chai. Catering has been offered, including live cooking stations for events.
tips: Try the biryani or samosa chaat, two frequently mentioned dishes.
Ask about catering with live cooking stations for parties.
Call ahead to confirm hours, since it has been closed on Mondays.

name: Whole Foods Market Avalon
desc: Avalon's anchor grocery store.
about: Whole Foods Market at Avalon is the development's grocery anchor, a roughly 48,000 square foot store at 2800 Old Milton Parkway that opened in October 2014 as one of the first Avalon tenants. It is open every day from 7am to 10pm.

Beyond the usual produce, meat, seafood and pantry aisles, the store has a hot bar and salad bar, a mochi bar, a bakery that takes custom cake orders, fresh pasta, grind-your-own nut butters, bulk spices and a cheese counter with a certified cheese professional. Prepared food counters include Market Sandwich, Genji Sushi and Poke Le Le, and The Main Brews and Bites serves coffee plus beer and wine by the glass, with cafe seating.
Amazon services are built in, including an Amazon Counter and free box-free returns. Prime members can also order grocery pickup or delivery.
tips: Drop off Amazon returns at the in-store counter, no box or label needed.
Order a custom cake from the bakery ahead of a party.
Grab a coffee, beer or glass of wine at The Main Brews and Bites while you shop Avalon.

name: Regal Avalon
desc: Avalon's 12-screen cinema with an RPX premium auditorium.
about: Regal Avalon is a 12-screen movie theater inside Avalon that opened in November 2014 alongside the development's first wave of shops and restaurants. One auditorium is an RPX premium large format screen.

Every auditorium is fitted with electric reclining seats with footrests and tables for eating, set in stadium rows for clear sight lines. The theater has trimmed its seat count over the years, to roughly 1,200 seats.

Along with popcorn and candy, the menu offers appetizers, entrees and desserts, and the lobby has a bar with lounge seating for a drink before or after the show. Avalon's restaurants and free parking decks are steps away, making it easy to pair a film with dinner.
tips: Buy tickets and pick seats ahead online, especially on weekends.
Look for RPX showtimes if you want the premium large format screen.
Park in the Avalon decks and have dinner at one of the nearby restaurants before the movie.

name: Apple Avalon
desc: Apple's retail store on Avalon's Boulevard.
about: Apple Avalon is the company's retail store at 8130 Avalon Boulevard, which took over from the former Apple store at North Point Mall when Apple moved its Alpharetta location to Avalon in 2017.

The store sells the full Apple lineup, from iPhone, iPad and Mac to Apple Watch and accessories, and staff can help set up new devices. The Genius Bar handles repairs and technical support by appointment, and free Today at Apple sessions cover creative and how-to topics.

Online orders can be picked up in store, and the Apple at Work team helps small businesses. Other services include in-person shopping sessions, Apple Vision Pro demos and sign language interpretation. It is open daily, with shorter hours on Sunday afternoons.
tips: Book Genius Bar appointments online before you go.
Choose in-store pickup when you order online to skip shipping.
Check the Today at Apple calendar for free sessions.

name: Anthropologie
desc: Anthropologie's Avalon store carries the brand's women's clothing, dresses, shoes and accessories alongside home goods such as decor, bedding, candles and tabletop pieces. It sits on Avalon's walkable main boulevard among other national retailers and restaurants, making it an easy stop on a shopping day.
tips: Browse the home section for gifts like candles and serveware.
Park in the Avalon decks and walk the boulevard.
Call ahead to confirm hours, especially around holidays.
about: Anthropologie's Avalon store at 4180 Avalon Boulevard carries the brand's women's clothing, dresses, shoes and accessories alongside home goods such as decor, bedding, candles and tabletop pieces.

It sits on Avalon's walkable main boulevard among other national retailers and restaurants, with parking in the development's decks, so it fits easily into a shopping day or an evening out. Store hours run from 10am on Monday through Saturday, with shorter Sunday hours.

name: Crate & Barrel
desc: Home furnishings anchor at Avalon.
about: Crate & Barrel's Alpharetta store sits at 1110 Avalon Boulevard, among the national retailers and restaurants that line Avalon's main street. Its Avalon storefront makes it an easy stop alongside other errands on the boulevard.

The store displays furniture alongside kitchenware, tabletop, decor, bedding and seasonal items, so you can see sofas and dining sets in person before ordering. Free design services are available by appointment: bring photos of your room and the design team will put together mood boards and layouts.
Crate & Barrel is also a popular wedding registry stop, and its Georgia stores host after-hours registry events with local wedding vendors. Parking is in the Avalon decks.
tips: Book a free design appointment and bring photos of the room you want to update.
Ask about after-hours registry events if you are planning a wedding.
Check current hours online, since they change by season.

name: lululemon
desc: lululemon's Avalon store sells technical athletic apparel and accessories for men and women, designed for running, training, yoga and everyday wear. It is set on Avalon Boulevard among the development's shops and restaurants, with staff on hand to help with fit and product questions.
tips: Ask staff for help with sizing between styles.
Sunday hours have been listed differently in some places, so confirm before a Sunday visit.
Park in the Avalon decks and combine the trip with other stops on the boulevard.
about: lululemon's Avalon store at 5185 Avalon Boulevard sells the brand's technical athletic apparel and accessories for men and women. The gear is designed for running, training and yoga as well as everyday wear, from leggings and shorts to jackets, bags and mats.

Staff on the floor can help with fit and product questions, which is useful when choosing between styles and fabrics. Online orders and the full catalog are available through the brand's website. It is a convenient stop for workout gear before a class at one of the fitness studios nearby.
The store sits on Avalon's main boulevard among the development's shops and restaurants, with parking in the nearby decks. It opens at 10am Monday through Saturday and keeps shorter hours on Sunday.

name: Life Time Alpharetta
desc: Large athletic country club with fitness floors, pools, tennis and pickleball on North Point Parkway.
about: Life Time Alpharetta is a large athletic club at 855 North Point Parkway. It is open from 4am to midnight on weekdays and 6am to 11pm on weekends, and the workout floor and studios host more than 100 group classes a week, from strength and cycle to yoga, Pilates and dance.

Swimmers have an indoor lap pool plus indoor and outdoor recreation pools, and there are indoor pickleball and basketball courts with leagues. Recovery options include a sauna and cold plunge, and LifeSpa offers hair, skin and nail services. LifeCafe serves a nutritionist-designed menu, and a Work Lounge gives members a place to work between sessions.
Families can use Kids Academy, which offers supervised childcare, kids classes, sports and camps. Membership is month to month, and the club offers free guided tours and day passes.
tips: Schedule a free guided tour online or by phone before joining.
Buy a day pass to try the club first.
Reserve popular group classes early through the member app.

name: Orangetheory Fitness Alpharetta
desc: Heart-rate-based group interval training studio on Old Milton Parkway.
about: Orangetheory Fitness Alpharetta is a group interval training studio at 3450 Old Milton Parkway, at the corner of North Point Parkway. It opened in 2014 as the brand's eighth Georgia location, under franchise owners Laura Salatino and Stacie Vaillancourt.

Classes are coach-led, total-body workouts that combine cardio and strength training, with HIIT and core-focused formats. Members wear heart-rate monitors so they can track effort zones on screens during class.

The studio is open daily from 5am to 9pm, with changing rooms and lockers. Classes are booked ahead, which makes it a structured option for people who like a set schedule and a coach to push them. Its corner spot at Old Milton and North Point Parkway puts it close to both Avalon and the North Point shopping district.
tips: Book classes ahead, since early morning and evening slots fill fast.
Arrive a little early for your first class so a coach can walk you through the equipment.
Holiday hours can change, so check with the studio before a holiday visit.

name: Song's Taekwondo Academy
desc: Longtime Alpharetta taekwondo school on Rucker Road.
about: Song's Taekwondo Academy is a martial arts school at 270 Rucker Road, Suite 200, in the Crabapple area of Alpharetta. Its roots trace back about 25 years to Gold Medal Taekwondo Academy in South Korea, founded by Master Tiger Song, before the school was established in Alpharetta.

Classes teach traditional taekwondo blended with elements of modern martial arts, with an emphasis on physical and mental discipline. The academy welcomes students of all ages and backgrounds, from beginners trying their first class to experienced martial artists, which makes it a common pick for kids' after-school activities.

The studio has a functional training area and a stretching area. Classes run on weekday afternoons and evenings, from 4pm to 8pm Monday, Tuesday, Thursday and Friday and until 7pm on Wednesday, and the school is closed on weekends.
tips: Plan around after-school timing, since classes run weekday afternoons and evenings only.

The practice sees children, adults and seniors for comprehensive eye exams and for diagnosis and management of eye diseases. It fits specialty contact lenses, including bifocal lenses for presbyopia, and sells eyeglasses and prescription sunglasses.

Patients considering LASIK or PRK can get pre-operative evaluations and follow-up care, and the doctors provide cataract diagnosis, surgical referrals and care before and after surgery. Saturday hours are offered at this Windward office.

name: Eye Associates of North Atlanta

about: Eye Associates of North Atlanta is the private ophthalmology practice of Dr. Anand K. Shah, a board-certified ophthalmologist and cataract surgeon with more than a decade of medical experience. The office is in Suite 94 at 5755 North Point Parkway, near North Point Mall between GA-400 exits 9 and 10.

The practice provides medical and surgical eye care for adults, including comprehensive eye exams, cataract surgery and care for glaucoma, diabetic eye disease, dry eye and macular degeneration. Dr. Shah performs each comprehensive exam himself and explains the results, and reviews often describe him as thorough.

Office hours run Monday through Friday from 9am to 5pm, with some evening and weekend times based on availability. The practice accepts most major insurance plans and offers a flat rate for self-pay patients.

Its physicians treat adults and children for sinus and nasal problems, allergies, sleep and snoring issues, voice and swallowing concerns and ear conditions. Pediatric otolaryngology is among the listed specialties, and audiologists are part of the team for hearing evaluations.

The practice's website includes background on each doctor's training and interests so patients know who they will see before a consultation. Call the office to make an appointment, or ask your doctor to send a referral.

The office treats adult and pediatric ENT conditions. Call (770) 740-1860 to confirm providers and hours before booking.

Wellstar's location page lists pediatric otolaryngologists Dr. Erik Bauer and Dr. Megan Ballard and otolaryngologist Dr. Paula Harmon at this office. Many families arrive through a pediatrician referral, so check whether your insurance requires one before calling (404) 255-2033.

about: Northside Hospital Orthopedics runs this sports medicine office in Building C, Suite 190, on the medical campus at 3400 Old Milton Parkway. The practice is part of the Northside Hospital system and focuses on bone, joint and sports injuries for both adults and young athletes.

Its listed specialties include hip and knee surgery, shoulder surgery, orthopedic sports medicine, pediatric sports medicine and non-operative orthopedics. Physicians named for this location are Dr. Jon Erik Minter, Dr. Christopher Potts and Dr. Joseph Powers, supported by physician assistants Deep Patel and Logan Pierce. Dr. Powers covers pediatric sports medicine and non-surgical care, while Dr. Minter and Dr. Potts handle surgical cases.
The office keeps weekday hours, 8am to 4:30pm Monday through Thursday, and closes earlier on Fridays at 2:30pm. Appointments are arranged by phone at (770) 663-1100.

about: PT Solutions calls this clinic Alpharetta Ellard, and it sits in Suite 480 at 8400 Holcomb Bridge Road, near the Ellard area and the Roswell line rather than on North Main Street. It is one clinic in the larger PT Solutions network and is listed as a service of Wellstar Windy Hill Hospital.

The clinic treats patients of all ages for orthopedic pain, sports injuries, pre and post surgery rehab, balance and dizziness problems, and neurological conditions. Across the company, services include dry needling, vestibular therapy, concussion care, pelvic floor therapy and occupational therapy, so it is worth asking which of these are offered at this location.

Hours run 7am to 7pm Monday through Thursday and 7am to 5pm on Friday, with weekends closed. The clinic can be reached by call or text at (770) 640-5470, and appointment requests can also be made online.

The clinic offers physical and occupational therapy, with services that include manual therapy, dry needling, concussion care, hand therapy, pre and post surgical rehab, sports physical therapy and telehealth visits. A first appointment starts with an evaluation, a plan of care and goal setting, and treatment can include exercise, hands-on techniques and a home program.

Office hours are Monday 7am to 4pm, Tuesday 8am to 6pm and Friday 7am to 1pm, with midweek hours posted on the clinic page. BenchMark works with most major insurance plans and also lists self-pay options and a complimentary screen.

about: North Atlanta Spine is a chiropractic office in Suite 96 at 5755 North Point Parkway. Its team of chiropractors and a massage therapist works with patients who have back pain, neck pain, headaches or muscle tightness, as well as people who want ongoing wellness care.

Services on the practice website include chiropractic adjustments, spinal decompression, massage therapy, soft tissue and myofascial therapy, assisted stretch therapy, and extracorporeal shockwave therapy (ESWT) for problems such as plantar fasciitis and tennis elbow. The office says it aims to make first visits easy for people who have never seen a chiropractor before.
The schedule changes through the week: Monday 8am to 5pm, Tuesday and Thursday 3pm to 6pm, Wednesday 8am to 1pm and Friday 9am to 3pm.

about: Northpoint Family Chiropractic Center has served the area since 1994 from Suite 101 at 3180 North Point Parkway. The practice is led by Dr. Colin, who has focused on sports care for 29 years, and it welcomes patients from infants to grandparents.

Alongside drug-free chiropractic care for the whole family, the office offers massage options ranging from a 15-minute chair massage to an hour of deep tissue work and a 90-minute lymphatic massage. Patient testimonials on the site describe families who have stayed with the practice for decades.

Office hours are Monday 10am to 5pm, Wednesday 10am to 7pm, Friday 10am to 3pm and Saturday 10am to noon. Tuesday and Thursday appointments from 3pm to 7pm are held at a home office, so confirm the location when booking.

about: Chiropractic Health Clinics, which also operates as Atlanta Chiropractic Group, is run by Dr. Alex Mahyar from Suite 750 at 2650 Holcomb Bridge Road. The practice describes a drug-free, hands-on approach to problems of the musculoskeletal and nervous systems.

Adjustment techniques include the Activator Method, Thompson Technique and Diversified Technique. The office also offers laser therapy, cupping, disc decompression, electro muscle therapy and ultrasound therapy, plus several types of massage such as deep tissue, hot stone, neuromuscular, sports and Swedish.

Patients recovering from car accidents can be treated as part of their personal injury management, and the practice describes its overall approach to neuromusculoskeletal complaints as holistic. Consultations are set up by calling (678) 381-1184, which is the best way to confirm current office hours.

about: Inner Compass Counseling is a group therapy practice with an Alpharetta office in Suite 227 at 5755 North Point Parkway, plus offices in Cumming and Marietta. Its therapists work with children ages 5 to 12, teens, young adults ages 18 to 30, individual adults, couples and families.

Specialties listed by the practice include EMDR, Dialectical Behavior Therapy (DBT), and support for anxiety and depression during pregnancy and postpartum. The practice describes therapy as a way to set goals, look at past patterns and build tools for handling life's challenges.

Sessions are available in person or through virtual counseling. Appointments are requested through the website form or by calling (770) 655-2484, and self-pay clients can ask for a Good Faith Estimate of costs.

Services include individual counseling, couples therapy, play therapy for children and EMDR. Office visits take place in Alpharetta, and online therapy is offered for clients in Georgia, California, Florida and South Carolina.

When you call, you speak with a therapist who helps match you with a counselor trained in what you need. The practice says it will point you to another resource if it is not the right fit. Evening, weekend and weekday appointments are available.

Treatments focus on injectables such as tox and filler, body contouring, laser and skin rejuvenation, facials, and the EMFACE device. The spa also offers medical wellness services, including hormone pellet therapy, testosterone replacement, IV therapy and peptides, which follow its prescription and medical evaluation policy. Medical-grade skincare and hair products are sold in the shop.
Visits start with a consultation. The spa is open Monday through Friday from 10am to 6pm and Saturday from 10am to 4pm.

Services cover skin renewal, injectables, laser hair removal, medical weight loss and bioidentical hormone replacement. Weight loss programs include in-person medical oversight.

The staff includes nurse practitioner Anna Carlise, physician assistant and injector Lauren Wages Edeker, PA-C, who directs aesthetics, and licensed esthetician Rachel Shah. Consultations are booked through the website or by calling (470) 470-9986.

name: Alpharetta High School
desc: Fulton County public high school, grades 9-12, on Webb Bridge Road.
about: Alpharetta High School is a Fulton County Schools public high school for grades 9 through 12 at 3595 Webb Bridge Road. It opened in 2004, and its teams are the Raiders, in maroon, silver and black.

The school offers the International Baccalaureate program, which it adopted in the 2018-19 school year, so students can pursue the full IB Diploma or take individual IB classes. Advanced Placement courses and dual enrollment are also available, along with band, orchestra, a music technology lab and dozens of student clubs. Its athletics history includes state titles in boys tennis, ice hockey and competition cheer.
Enrollment topped 2,000 students in recent years. The main office can be reached at (470) 254-7640, and attendance is based on the district's zone maps.

name: Innovation Academy

about: Innovation Academy is a Fulton County Schools magnet high school for grades 9 through 12 at 125 Milton Avenue in downtown Alpharetta. Students follow a career pathway alongside a STEM and humanities program built around design thinking and research.

The school's stated vision is to develop innovative leaders, and its mission stresses solving real-world problems through research. Students complete magnet program requirements on top of Georgia graduation requirements, and offerings include Advanced Placement classes, a health science pathway, a research program, biliteracy seals, and sports and clubs.
The school day runs from 8:20am to 4:00pm. Rising 9th graders go through a pathway declaration process, and the school hosts information sessions for families.

name: Milton High School

about: Milton High School is a Fulton County public high school for grades 9 through 12 at 13025 Birmingham Highway in Milton, across from Northwestern Middle School. The Eagles serve north Alpharetta and Milton neighborhoods.

The school traces its history to 1921, when it opened near Main Street in Alpharetta to serve Milton County, and it is marking 100 years. An FFA-built log cabin from its early days still stands as a memorial, and the school later became Fulton County's first comprehensive high school. A growing student body and a land-locked downtown campus led the district to build the current campus around an academy model.
Today it offers AP courses, dual enrollment, chorus, orchestra, theatre and a wide range of clubs and athletics. The main office number is (470) 254-7000.

name: Cambridge High School

about: Cambridge High School is a Fulton County public high school for grades 9 through 12 on Bethany Bend in Milton. It opened in August 2012, drawing students from both Alpharetta and Milton.

The site sits on land once owned by the Cogburn family in the old Bethany community. Wetlands run through the campus, and the bridge built to cross them became a symbol of the school joining two cities. Students chose the Bears as the mascot, with navy blue, Carolina blue and white as school colors.

Academic offerings include AP courses, career and technical pathways, national language honor societies and a counseling team that supports college planning. Band, chorus, clubs and a full athletic program round out student life. New families start with the enrollment pages on the school website.

name: Webb Bridge Middle School
