about: Webb Bridge Middle School is a Fulton County public middle school for grades 6 through 8 at 4455 Webb Bridge Road. It opened on September 3, 1996, about two miles east of Highway 400.

The school is named for the Webb families who have lived in the area since the 1840s, including Reverend John M. Webb, a preacher and teacher whose bridge over Big Creek gave the road its name. The building was designed for about 1,325 students and includes science and computer labs, band, chorus and orchestra rooms, art rooms, a video journalism lab, a gym with a stage, a track, tennis courts and athletic fields.
Each grade takes on a service learning project, and the school has earned Common Sense School recognition for digital citizenship.

about: Haynes Bridge Middle School is a Fulton County public middle school for grades 6 through 8 at 10665 Haynes Bridge Road. It opened in 1983 on 30 acres that were once part of Richard Luther Haynes Jr.'s plantation, and it was expanded in 1989 and 2007.

Students come from Barnwell, Hillside, Mimosa and Northwood elementary schools and move on to Centennial High School. Electives that can earn high school credit include computer science, audio video film, visual arts, orchestra, band and chorus. The campus has a football field, track and tennis courts.

A restored chimney from the late 1700s Haynes plantation stands near the school garden, moved there from GA 400 and Haynes Bridge Road in 2000. Classes run from 8:55am to 4:05pm, with breakfast served beforehand.

name: Holcomb Bridge Middle School

about: Holcomb Bridge Middle School is a Fulton County public middle school for grades 6 through 8 at 2700 Holcomb Bridge Road, close to the Roswell line. It calls itself The School of Global Classrooms and is part of the Northeast Learning Community, feeding Centennial High School.

With an average enrollment of about 530, it is a smaller middle school than many in the area. The school has been named a Lighthouse School to Watch, and it offers talented and gifted services, French for students on that pathway, a reading bowl team, literacy nights in English and Spanish, clubs and athletics.
Students can arrive at 8:25am for breakfast, classes start at 8:55am and dismissal is at 4:05pm. Walkers and car riders leave first, followed by bus riders.

name: Hopewell Middle School

about: Hopewell Middle School is a Fulton County public middle school for grades 6 through 8 at 13060 Cogburn Road in Milton. It opened in 2004, and its mascot is the Mustang, with red and silver as school colors.

Average enrollment is about 1,200 students. Feeder elementary schools include Alpharetta, Birmingham Falls, Cogburn, Manning Oaks and Summit Hill, and students go on to Alpharetta High, Cambridge High or Innovation Academy. The school is a No Place for Hate campus and has a bilingual community liaison for families.

Recent highlights posted by the school include a robotics design award, a DECA team at state, orchestra performances at senior centers and band caroling at local elementary schools. The school day runs roughly 8:50am to 4:05pm.

name: Alpharetta Elementary School

about: Alpharetta Elementary School is a Fulton County public elementary school at 192 Mayfield Road near downtown Alpharetta. It serves pre-kindergarten through 5th grade, with an average enrollment of about 513 students, and is celebrating its 70th anniversary.

Special programs include special education, talented and gifted services and ESOL. The school partners with ArtsNOW to bring STEAM lessons into K-5 classrooms, and students have teamed up with Innovation Academy on a mini-boat ocean tracking project. It lists a 5 Star Climate Rating among its recognitions.
Graduates feed into Hopewell or Northwestern middle schools and then Cambridge or Milton high schools. The school day runs from 7:40am to 2:20pm, and doors open at 7:10am.

about: Creek View Elementary is a Fulton County public school for kindergarten through 5th grade at 3995 Webb Bridge Road. Home of the Cheetahs, it enrolls about 750 students who represent more than 15 countries, and its colors are navy blue and hunter green.

Students can qualify for talented and gifted (TAG), special education and ESOL services. Extracurriculars include chorus, a school musical, ukulele, student council, Science Olympiad and yearbook club, and the PTA helps fund enrichment programs. The school's PAWS behavior program asks students to keep a positive attitude, accept responsibility, make wise choices and put safety first.
Creek View students go on to Webb Bridge Middle School and Alpharetta High School. The school day runs from 7:40am to 2:20pm, and families can sign up for a school tour through the website.

about: Lake Windward Elementary is a Fulton County public elementary school at 11770 East Fox Court in the Windward area. The Gators wear green and navy blue, and the school motto is Learn and Grow, Lead and Show.

Students in kindergarten through 5th grade have access to special education, including self-contained classes, as well as bilingual parent support and school-based mental health services. After school, families can choose from Y afterschool care and enrichment programs such as Challenge Island STEAM, Kid Create Studio art and Premier Martial Arts. Fourth and fifth graders take part in a tech fair, and the school lists a 2026 Double Platinum award and a Ready Georgia Seal of Preparedness.
Rising 6th graders head to Webb Bridge or Taylor Road middle schools. Arrival starts at 7:10am, and classes run until 2:20pm.

The school serves pre-kindergarten through 5th grade, including a special needs Pre-K. Its PTA and School Governance Council organize programs such as STEAM Day and a mentoring program, and family events through the year include a Back to School Bash, the Shamrock Shindig and Taste of New Prospect. Its motto is Grow, Celebrate, Matter.
After 5th grade, students move on to Webb Bridge Middle School and Alpharetta High School. The school day runs from 7:40am to 2:20pm.

Clubs and activities include an academic team, a beautification and gardening club, Girls on the Run, a kindness club, Science Olympiad and student council. The school also offers talented and gifted services, extended learning and after-school programs, and one of its ESOL teachers was named an exemplary ESOL teacher by Fulton County Schools.
Graduates go on to Hopewell or Northwestern middle schools. Morning arrival runs from 7:10am to 7:35am, the tardy bell rings at 7:40am, and dismissal is at 2:20pm.

name: Fulton Science Academy
desc: STEM-focused private school, PK-12, on Fanfare Way.
about: Fulton Science Academy is a private STEM school for Pre-K through 12th grade at 3035 Fanfare Way. The school says it is designed for advanced and gifted learners, and its core values go by the name I CARE.

Academics run through elementary, middle and high school divisions, with gifted education, STEAM labs, character education and college counseling. Students also take part in visual and performing arts, competitive academic teams, clubs and a range of sports for the Mustangs.

The school has been recognized as a National Blue Ribbon School and a National School of Character by Character.org, and it was named a 2025 Cognia School of Distinction. Niche ranked it first in Georgia for STEM high schools in its 2027 rankings. Prospective families can attend open houses, with separate sessions for Pre-K through 5th grade and for grades 6 through 12.
tips: Register for the open house that matches your child's grade level
Tuition, fees and financial aid details are on the admissions pages
Call (678) 366-2555 to arrange a visit

name: Fusion Academy Alpharetta
desc: One-to-one private school for grades 4-12 at Avalon.
about: Fusion Academy Alpharetta is an accredited private school for grades 4 through 12 in Suite 150 at 10000 Avalon Boulevard. Most classes pair one student with one teacher, and the model is aimed at students with learning, social or emotional differences.

Students can attend full time or take individual courses for credit, choosing from more than 300 classes, which some families use to catch up or recover credits. Instruction can be in person or virtual, small group classes hold two to five students, and self-directed digital sessions build independent study skills. The Homework Café and social clubs give students time with peers, and families receive progress reports from teachers every school day.
The campus accepts the Georgia Special Needs Scholarship and the Georgia Promise Scholarship. It is open weekdays from 7:30am to 7:30pm.
tips: Ask admissions how the Georgia Special Needs or Promise scholarships apply
Single courses for credit are an option without enrolling full time
Look for Suite 150 at 10000 Avalon Boulevard

name: Alpharetta Christian Academy
desc: Private Christian school and a ministry of First City Church, located on Academy Street in downtown Alpharetta. It serves children from age 2 through 5th grade, with a preschool program and an elementary curriculum that includes Bible, phonics and cursive starting in first grade.
tips: Schedule a tour before applying
Applications can be submitted online through the school website
Call (770) 475-5762 with enrollment questions
about: Alpharetta Christian Academy is a private Christian school at 44 Academy Street in downtown Alpharetta, run as a ministry of First City Church. It serves children from age 2 through 5th grade.

The preschool program works on cognitive, fine motor, gross motor and social and emotional skills, while the elementary grades follow a traditional academic curriculum with Christian teaching. Classes are kept small, with a 12 to 1 student to teacher ratio, and the school stresses close partnerships with families. It is accredited through the Georgia Accrediting Commission.

The school describes its aim as giving each child a spiritual and academic foundation for lifelong learning. Families can apply online, and staff answer questions about the school and the application process by phone at (770) 475-5762.

name: Holy Redeemer Catholic School
desc: Catholic school, PK-8, on Old Alabama Road.
address: 3380 Old Alabama Rd, Johns Creek, GA 30022
about: Holy Redeemer Catholic School is a parochial school for Pre-K 4 through 8th grade at 3380 Old Alabama Road, an address now within the City of Johns Creek. It opened on September 7, 1999, as one of three new Catholic elementary schools in the Atlanta archdiocese that year.

The school describes itself as a faith-centered community rooted in Catholic tradition with a focus on academics and lifelong learning. Its facilities include a STREAM lab and a recently opened full-day Pre-K 4 classroom. Community traditions over the years have included Grandparents Day, an alumni luncheon and fundraising events such as a golf tournament and gala.
Prospective families can attend First Look preview events, which include a presentation from school leaders and a tour of classrooms. The enrollment office is reached at (770) 410-4056.
tips: Sign up for a First Look preview through the school's Come Visit page
Use a Johns Creek address in your GPS
Call the enrollment office at (770) 410-4056

name: King's Ridge Christian School
desc: Christian college-prep school, K-12, on Bethany Bend.
about: King's Ridge Christian School is a private Christian college preparatory school at 2765 Bethany Bend. It enrolls more than 885 students from Pre-K through 12th grade.

The school is organized into a Lower School for Pre-K through 4th grade, a Middle School for grades 5 through 8 and a High School for grades 9 through 12. It describes a whole-child approach in which faculty challenge and mentor students, with a rigorous academic program grounded in Christian faith.

Families considering the school are encouraged to visit the campus and meet faculty and students. Admissions questions go to the main office at (770) 754-5738, and the school publishes its 2025 to 2030 strategic plan on its website.
tips: Schedule a campus visit to see the division your child would join
Lower School begins with Pre-K
Call (770) 754-5738 for admissions questions

name: Mill Springs Academy
desc: K-12 school for students with learning differences, on New Providence Road.
about: Mill Springs Academy is an independent school on New Providence Road for students in grades 1 through 12 with ADHD, autism spectrum disorder, language-based learning differences and anxiety. Its guiding idea is that if a student cannot learn the way a school teaches, the school should teach the way the student learns.

Instruction combines hands-on, project-based learning with individualized support from a team of specialists, aiming to build academic, executive functioning, social and emotional skills. The school calls its goal Real World Ready, preparing graduates for four-year colleges, arts programs, the workforce or a gap year. A college preparatory track is offered.
Students come from more than 50 ZIP codes around metro Atlanta, and a bus program makes stops across the region. The school also runs an E4 program and a one-to-one device program.
tips: Ask admissions about bus routes, since stops serve the wider metro area
Grades start at 1st grade, not kindergarten
Look into the late bus option if your student stays for activities

name: St. Francis Schools - Alpharetta
desc: Private school on Cogburn Road, best known for its high school.
about: Saint Francis School is an independent private school founded in 1976 with two campuses. The Cogburn Road location is its Milton Campus, which serves grades 4 through 12 after expanding for the 2026-27 school year, while a Roswell campus covers kindergarten through 8th grade.

The school offers a college preparatory program with AP courses for students with a range of academic abilities, and it places weight on individual attention, with a 7 to 1 student to teacher ratio. Dyslexia and structured literacy support is part of its academic program.

Outside class, students take part in visual and performing arts and a full athletic program, and families from both campuses come together at events such as an annual Family Night. Prospective families can contact admissions through the website or by phone.
tips: Use the Milton address on Cogburn Road for the upper school campus
Younger students may attend the Roswell campus instead
Ask about dyslexia and structured literacy support during admissions

name: McGinnis Woods Country Day School
desc: Private school on Faircroft Drive that has served Alpharetta families since 1999, from infant and toddler care through private Pre-K and grades K-8. It is NAEYC, Cognia and Georgia Accrediting Commission accredited and offers before and after school programs.
tips: Attend an open house, such as the one scheduled for January 30, 2027
Ask to see a Day in the Life visit to observe small classes
Ask about Discovery Clubs if you need after-school activities
about: McGinnis Woods Country Day School has served families since 1999 from its campus on Faircroft Drive. It covers infant and toddler care, preschool and Pre-K, and private school through 8th grade, drawing families from Alpharetta, Johns Creek and south Forsyth County.

The curriculum is described as hands-on and minds-on rather than textbook driven, with an emphasis on STEM, technology and robotics, plus arts, clubs and community service. Frequent field trips and overnight excursions reinforce classroom lessons. Teacher to student ratios are 9 to 1 in Pre-K 4 and Pre-K 5 and 11 to 1 from kindergarten through 8th grade.

Middle school students can play volleyball, soccer, basketball and track and field, and after-school Discovery Clubs cover arts, science, robotics and athletics. The school holds open houses for prospective families.

name: Alpharetta International Academy
desc: Nonsectarian Montessori school founded in 1981 on Webb Bridge Road, serving children from 18 months through grade 8. Programs run from pre-primary and primary/kindergarten through elementary and middle school, with Spanish taught daily from kindergarten.
tips: Book a tour or attend an open house before applying
Students can stay from toddler years through 8th grade
The office is open weekdays from 8am to 4pm
about: Alpharetta International Academy is a private, nonprofit Montessori school that has operated on Webb Bridge Road since 1981. It serves children from 18 months through 8th grade on a wooded campus of more than five acres.

Programs run from pre-primary through primary and kindergarten, elementary and middle school, each set up as a multi-age classroom guided by Montessori-trained teachers. A Spanish program, enrichment classes and summer camps round out the offerings, and extended day and after-school activities are available for working families. Many teachers have been with the school for a decade or longer.

Families from more than 30 countries are part of the school community. The school's guiding principles are kindness, diversity and innovation, and its outdoor spaces are used as an extension of the classroom.

name: Crabapple Montessori School
desc: Montessori school, preschool through grade 6, in Crabapple.
about: Crabapple Montessori School is a private preschool and elementary school at 12387 Crabapple Road for children ages 15 months to 12 years. It is accredited by Cognia and follows an authentic Montessori curriculum.

Classes are grouped into toddler (15 months to 3 years), primary (3 to 6 years) and elementary (6 to 12 years) levels. The school sits on a three-acre wooded lot, and the building was designed around Montessori principles, with spacious, naturally lit classrooms. Each classroom has its own fenced children's garden for outdoor learning.

Families come from Alpharetta, Milton, Roswell, Cumming, Canton and Woodstock. Admission follows a set path: schedule a tour, submit an application, attend a parent interview, bring your child for a visit, and then receive a decision.
tips: Start the admissions process by scheduling a tour
Plan for a parent interview and a child visit before a decision
Children can start as young as 15 months

name: The Goddard School - Windward
desc: Franchise preschool on Windward Parkway, part of The Goddard School network, offering early childhood programs through pre-K. Enrichment listed for this school includes STEAM, robotics, a rock wall, Spanish, world cultures, and yoga and mindfulness.
tips: Schedule a tour early, since availability is limited
Open weekdays from 7am to 6pm
Ask about enrichment classes like yoga, Spanish and chess
about: The Goddard School of Alpharetta, Windward is a franchise preschool and daycare at 4875 Windward Parkway. It follows Goddard's Wonder of Learning program, which was developed with early childhood experts and centers on children's natural curiosity.

The school describes a whole-child approach that covers academic growth, emotional development, social skills and gross motor skills, with small ratios in its classrooms. Enrichment classes include yoga, Spanish and chess, and teachers build personalized lesson plans. The school recognizes its staff with awards such as an annual Teacher of the Year.
Hours are 7am to 6pm on weekdays, which suits families who need full-day care. The school currently notes limited availability, so families are encouraged to schedule a tour early.

name: The Goddard School - Holcomb Bridge
desc: Franchise preschool on Holcomb Bridge Road, listed by Goddard as The Goddard School of Roswell - Holcomb Bridge despite its Alpharetta address. It offers play-based early childhood programs focused on hands-on learning, exploration and social skills.
tips: Search for the Roswell, Holcomb Bridge name on Goddard's site
The school reports immediate openings for infants, toddlers and preschoolers
Open weekdays from 7am to 6pm
about: Goddard lists this franchise preschool at 2710 Holcomb Bridge Road as The Goddard School of Roswell, Holcomb Bridge, even though the address is in Alpharetta. Krupal and Jessy Singh have owned the school since August 2023, and Krupal, a former teacher with degrees in early childhood education, works on site with families and staff.

The school uses Goddard's Wonder of Learning program, and its vision stresses empathy, inclusion and belonging, with hands-on learning, exploration and problem solving for children of all ages. It is currently enrolling infants, toddlers and preschoolers and reports immediate openings.
Hours are 7am to 6pm on weekdays, and tours can be scheduled through the Goddard website or by calling (770) 993-3307.

name: Carrington Academy Alpharetta
desc: Carrington Academy's Alpharetta Avalon campus on Webb Bridge Road, part of a small north metro Atlanta preschool group. It offers daycare and preschool from 6 weeks through Pre-K, plus before and after care and summer camp, using a play-based Links to Learning curriculum.
tips: Call or use Request Information to confirm hours and openings
Ask whether a Georgia Pre-K seat is available for your child's age
Before and after care plus summer camp are offered
about: Carrington Academy's Alpharetta, Avalon campus on Webb Bridge Road is part of a small group of north metro Atlanta preschools, with other locations in Cumming, Suwanee and Braselton. The company was founded in 2001 by Valerie and Chris Davis in Gainesville, Georgia.

Programs cover infants, toddlers, preschool, Pre-K and Georgia Pre-K, plus before and after school care and summer camp. The Links to Learning curriculum builds literacy, math, art, science and social skills step by step, and teachers adjust lessons to each child's interests and learning style.
Carrington is part of Spring Education Group. Families can call or use the Request Information form to check current openings and hours at this campus.

name: Montessori Scholars Academy
desc: Nonsectarian Montessori school founded in 2011 on Morris Road, listed with a Milton address on its own site. It runs infant, toddler and primary programs with an elementary level, small classes averaging about 8 students, and lead guides with Montessori training.
tips: Book a tour through the school website
Summer camp is offered
Ask about timing for the planned elementary program
about: Montessori Scholars Academy is a private Montessori school at 13100 Morris Road, listed with a Milton address on its own website. It follows the method developed by Maria Montessori, focusing on independence, self-motivation and a love of learning.

Current programs include infant, toddler and primary classes, with an elementary program listed as coming soon. Primary classrooms are organized into four areas of learning: practical life, sensory, language and mathematics. Children work through hands-on activities at their own pace, and the school says its staff take part in ongoing training.
The school holds SACS (now Cognia) accreditation and offers a summer camp. Families can schedule a visit by calling (770) 754-0777 or through the website.

name: Amasa Mexican Kitchen
desc: Coastal Mexican spot in Alpharetta City Center from Juan Calle, co-creator of Chicheria Mexican Kitchen and Buena Vida Tapas. The whole menu is gluten-free, with house-made organic blue corn tortillas, ceviches, Baja fish tacos and a whole crispy snapper. It opened in August 2026 in the former Jekyll Brewing space and has a rooftop bar.
tips: Groups of nine or more should book through the private dining page
Come for the weekday happy hour from 4pm to 6pm
Sunday brunch is a buffet from 11am to 3pm
about: Amasa Mexican Kitchen is a Baja California inspired restaurant at 15 Academy Street in Alpharetta City Center, and a sister concept to Chichería Mexican Kitchen. The entire menu is gluten-free, and blue corn tortillas are pressed fresh every day.

The menu leans toward seafood, with ceviche and crudos, Baja fish tacos and other gourmet tacos, sweet corn esquites, carne asada fries and fajitas. The bar focuses on tequila and mezcal, with margarita flights and seasonal margaritas, and there is a rooftop bar.

Lunch is served weekdays from 11am to 3pm, dinner nightly, and a brunch buffet runs Sundays from 11am to 3pm. The weekly lineup includes a weekday happy hour from 4pm to 6pm, Family Night Mondays, trivia on Tuesdays, wine and live jazz on the rooftop Wednesdays, and a late-night lounge on Saturdays.

name: Chuan Tasty
desc: Sichuan restaurant on Windward Parkway that pairs fiery Chengdu-style cooking with American Chinese favorites. Regulars point to the Dan Dan noodles, Mongolian beef, salt and pepper prawns, steamed pork buns and grilled skewers, and the drink list includes Taiwanese, Thai and taro milk teas. Dine-in, takeout and delivery are all offered.
tips: Order directly through the restaurant website for takeout or delivery
Dine-in tables spending $35 or more can get a free cold noodle dish while the offer lasts
Try the grilled skewers if you want something beyond the classics
about: Chuan Tasty is a Chinese restaurant in Suite 440 at 5530 Windward Parkway that pairs Sichuan cooking in the fiery Chengdu style with familiar American Chinese dishes.

The menu runs from dumplings, bao buns, stir-fries and soups to Peking duck, Kung Pao chicken and broccoli shrimp. Grilled skewers are a draw, including beef, lamb, beef tendon and tofu skin, and diners who like more traditional Sichuan food can find dishes such as iron plate squid and pork intestine. Reviews on the restaurant's site often mention the steamed pork buns.
You can dine in, order takeout or get delivery, and online ordering is available directly through the website. The restaurant is open every day from 11am to 10pm.

name: Thai Candle Seafood & Bar
desc: Upscale but relaxed Thai restaurant at Avalon led by a chef from northern Thailand, with a menu built around fresh seafood. The coastal trio of seared grouper, shrimp and scallops in a coconut sauce is a signature, and desserts include Thai tea creme brulee and green tea cheesecake. A full bar pours wine and cocktails.
tips: Dress business casual for dinner; athletic wear and hats are not allowed
The weekday lunch menu runs from 11:30am to 3pm
Reserve online, especially for weekend evenings at Avalon
about: Thai Candle Seafood & Bar serves modern Thai food at 7140 Avalon Boulevard, with a menu built around fresh seafood, steak and signature cocktails. Its first location is at The Forum in Peachtree Corners.

Expect a sleek dining room and dishes that lean on coastal seafood, including some served with a tableside presentation. The dinner menu is available all day, a lunch menu runs Monday through Friday from 11:30am to 3pm except holidays, and a full bar pours wine and cocktails. The restaurant also hosts private parties and corporate events.

At dinner, guests are asked to follow a business casual dress code, and athletic wear, sweatpants and hats are not allowed. Hours are 11:30am to 10pm Sunday through Thursday and until 10:30pm on Friday and Saturday. Reservations, online ordering and gift cards are available through the website.

name: Five Daughters Bakery Avalon
desc: Avalon outpost of the family-run Franklin, Tennessee bakery owned by Isaac and Stephanie Meek and their five daughters. It is known for the croissant-style 100 Layer Donut in full and mini sizes, alongside yeast-raised donuts with vegan options, paleo donuts made with gluten-free ingredients, pastries and coffee, all made from scratch daily.
tips: Check the bakery's website for current Avalon hours before you go
Go earlier in the day for the best selection of 100 Layer Donuts
Ask the staff which 100 Layer Donut flavors are in the case that day
about: Five Daughters Bakery has an Avalon shop at 200 Avalon Boulevard, one of its locations in Tennessee and Georgia. The family business was started in 2015 by Isaac and Stephanie Meek in their home in Franklin, Tennessee, and is named for the couple's five daughters.

The bakery is best known for its 100 Layer Donut, a tall, croissant-style pastry that takes three days to make from start to finish. Other donuts, pastries and coffee fill out the counter, and the 100 Layer Donut is the item most closely tied to the brand.

The company is now based in Nashville and opened its first Georgia shop in Atlanta in 2018 before expanding around the metro area. Its Avalon page is part of the bakery's official website, where you can check current details before visiting.

name: Where's The Scoop
type: Ice cream and bubble tea shop
desc: Dessert bar in Alpharetta City Center that freezes customizable small-batch ice cream to order, in both dairy and vegan versions, with seasonal ingredients and fresh fruit. It also makes bubble tea from brewed tea and ground spices, from taro and Thai tea to rose and vegan horchata, with boba, popping pearls and Oreo toppings, plus coffee.
tips: Closed Mondays, and it opens at 5pm Tuesday through Thursday
Vegan ice cream makes it an easy stop for mixed groups
Weekend hours start at 1pm, so it works for an afternoon treat
address: 26 Old Roswell St, Ste 102, Alpharetta, GA 30009
about: Where's The Scoop is a neighborhood dessert cafe at 26 Old Roswell Street, Suite 102, in downtown Alpharetta, with a second shop in Holly Springs. It serves rolled ice cream, bubble tea and coffee, all made from scratch.

The ice cream comes in both farm-fresh dairy and vegan versions, and it is frozen in front of you, which makes the visit something to watch. You build a small-batch order from a long list of mix-ins, seasonal ingredients and fresh fruit, and new recipes rotate in with the seasons and locally sourced ingredients.

Bubble teas are made with brewed teas and freshly ground spices, in flavors from taro and Thai tea to rose and vegan horchata. Boba is made fresh through the day, and toppings include popping pearls and Oreo crumbles.

name: Kilwins Alpharetta
type: Chocolate, fudge and ice cream shop
desc: Locally owned Kilwins confectionery on Market Street in Alpharetta City Center. It sells Mackinac Island fudge, super-premium ice cream, caramel corn and brittle made in copper kettles, hand-dipped caramel apples and Dubai chocolate, and guests can watch small-batch chocolates and fudge being made in the shop.
tips: Stop by in the afternoon to watch fudge and chocolate being made
Open until 10pm on Friday and Saturday for an after-dinner treat
Make sure your map points to 251 Market Street
about: Kilwins Alpharetta is a chocolate, fudge and ice cream shop at 251 Market Street in downtown Alpharetta. It is part of the Kilwins confectionery brand, which traces its chocolate making back more than 75 years.

Inside, you can watch small-batch treats being made. The shop sells Mackinac Island fudge, Original Recipe ice cream, Heritage Chocolate in milk, dark and white, and Dubai chocolate. Caramel apples start with Granny Smith apples hand-dipped in caramel made in the store, then finished plain, in chocolate or with nuts and sprinkles. Caramel corn and brittle are cooked in traditional copper kettles.
The shop opens at noon every day and stays open until 9pm Monday through Thursday, 10pm on Friday and Saturday, and 8pm on Sunday. Gift boxes are available for holidays and special occasions.

name: Lava Island Alpharetta
desc: Indoor play park with tall slides, foam pits, trampolines, obstacle courses, climbing areas and a separate toddler zone, plus glow-in-the-dark themed party rooms. There is no age limit and parents can play too. A full kitchen serves food, sweets, milkshakes and specialty coffee. Passes are sold by the hour or for the full day.
tips: Every adult must sign a waiver, so do it online before you arrive
Socks are required; bring your own or buy a pair there
Sign up for the loyalty program at the register to earn free all-day passes
about: Lava Island Alpharetta is a large indoor playground at 7121 North Point Parkway with slides, foam pits, trampolines and climbing areas, plus a dedicated toddler area for crawlers and younger children. There is no age limit, and parents are welcome to play too.

Everyone who goes past the lobby needs a wristband, with one-hour and all-day passes available and adult admission set at half the child rate. Infants 11 months and younger get in free. No reservation is needed, and all-day pass holders can leave and come back the same day. A full kitchen serves food and premium coffee.

Birthday parties use glow-in-the-dark themed party rooms, and adjusted rates are available for schools, churches and camps. The park is open daily from 9am to 9pm, staying open until 10pm on Fridays and Saturdays.

name: Play Street Museum Alpharetta
desc: Pretend-play museum for ages 1 to 8 built like a miniature city, with a cafe, doctor's office, fire truck and block area, plus an art station, slime lab and a rotating Discovery Rug exhibit. Weekly themes cover notable people, holidays and cultures, and weekend events include pottery, canvas painting and dino digs.
tips: Reserve a weekday session online before you go
Food is not allowed in the play area, but drinks are welcome
Check the events calendar for weekend playtimes
address: 11770 Haynes Bridge Rd, Ste 701-702, Alpharetta, GA 30009
about: Play Street Museum Alpharetta is a small-scale, interactive children's museum at 11770 Haynes Bridge Road, Suites 701 and 702. It is designed like a miniature city for children ages 1 to 8, who can take orders at a pretend cafe, get a checkup at the doctor's office, ride the play fire truck or build with blocks.

Parents can play alongside their kids or sit back while they explore. Playtime is by reservation on weekdays, with five 90-minute sessions each day starting at 8:30am, 10:30am, 12:30pm, 2:30pm and 4:30pm. Weekend playtimes and special events are posted separately.
The museum can also be booked for private birthday parties, playdates and school field trips. Older and younger siblings get in free with a paying child, though older kids are asked to play calmly.

name: The Slime Factory Alpharetta
desc: Hands-on slime lab inside North Point Mall where kids mix two custom slimes with toppings and scents, then try a gooey sensory pool, a slime wall and photo spots before leaving with a Master Slime Maker certificate. Sessions run 30 to 60 minutes, and the 5,000-square-foot space also hosts birthday parties and field trips.
tips: Everyone should sign the online waiver before arriving
Tickets are required for ages 2 and up, and kids under 14 need an adult
Booking a ticket gets you a coupon toward a birthday party package
address: 1000 North Point Cir, Ste 1082, Alpharetta, GA 30022
about: The Slime Factory runs a hands-on slime lab inside North Point Mall, in Suite 1082 at 1000 North Point Circle. Kids put on lab coats and safety goggles, mix their own batches at the lab bench and test how far the slime will stretch.

General admission sessions last 30 to 60 minutes and include two custom slimes, protective gear, a sensory pool, a certificate and photo spots. Birthday parties come in two sizes, small for 5 to 12 slime makers and large for 13 to 25, and run two hours. Field trips for 15 to 50 children are offered on weekdays and last 90 minutes.
The lab is open 11am to 7pm Monday through Thursday, 11am to 8pm on Friday and Saturday, and noon to 7pm on Sunday. Holiday hours may differ.

name: Camp Bow Wow Alpharetta
desc: Dog daycare, overnight boarding, grooming and enrichment center with indoor and outdoor play yards. Owners can watch their dogs on live webcams and manage bookings in the Camp app. Boarding cabins come with a cot, fleece blanket and nightly treat, and medication and daytime play during a stay are included rather than billed as extras.
tips: Call (678) 679-1964 to schedule your dog's interview
Claim the first-day-free offer on the website for new campers
Early weekday drop-off starts at 6:45am
address: 1755 Grassland Pkwy, Ste E, Alpharetta, GA 30004
about: Camp Bow Wow Alpharetta offers dog daycare, overnight boarding, grooming and enrichment from Suite E at 1755 Grassland Parkway in the Windward area. Dogs play in indoor and outdoor yards, and owners can check in on them through live webcams on a computer or phone.

Boarding guests sleep in individual cabins with a cot, a fleece blanket and a nightly treat. Giving medication carries no extra charge, and neither does daycare play during a boarding stay. The Camp app lets owners manage camper profiles, request reservations and view the webcams.
Every new dog has to pass an interview and meet entrance requirements before its first visit. The center opens at 6:45am on weekdays and 7am on weekends, closing at 7pm every day.

name: Wills Park Vet
desc: General practice animal hospital in the Haynes Bridge Road shopping center offering wellness exams, dental care, spay and neuter surgery, in-house lab work, a pharmacy and travel health certificates. It also offers same-day and drop-off appointments, plans tailored to each pet, and free Happy Visits that help nervous pets get used to the clinic.
tips: Call (678) 369-6843 for emergencies instead of booking online
Ask about a free Happy Visit for an anxious pet
For after-hours care, check the clinic's Emergency Partners list
address: 11770 Haynes Bridge Rd, Ste 703, Alpharetta, GA 30009
about: Wills Park Vet is a general practice animal hospital in Suite 703 at 11770 Haynes Bridge Road. Dr. Drew Keller leads the practice and schedules unhurried appointments so owners have time to ask questions.

Services include wellness and preventive exams, dental care, spay and neuter surgery, in-house diagnostic lab work, a pharmacy and health certificates for pets traveling in the US or abroad. Wellness plans are tailored to each pet's age, breed and lifestyle, and same-day and drop-off appointments help busy owners.

The clinic uses gentle handling to keep visits calm, and it offers free Happy Visits so nervous pets can get to know the staff and building. Appointments and messages go through the Digitail app. Hours are 7:30am to 5:30pm on weekdays.

name: Pit Stop for Pets
type: Dog groomer and self-serve dog wash
desc: Independent pet shop in Crabapple, open more than 14 years, that combines professional grooming with self-serve dog wash stations and USA-made food and treats. Grooming visits double as coat health checks, with staff reviewing the coat, skin, ears and body and reporting what they find. It sits behind the historic Silos landmark.
tips: Self-wash happy hour is a $15 flat rate for any size dog, Tuesday to Thursday 3pm to 5pm
Closed Mondays
Book grooming on a four to six week routine
about: Pit Stop for Pets is an independent dog grooming shop in Suite 154 at 12315 Crabapple Road, where it has operated for more than 14 years. It serves dogs from Alpharetta, Milton and Roswell, combining professional grooming, self-serve wash stations and USA-made food and treats under one roof.

Each grooming visit doubles as a coat health treatment: staff work through the coat, skin, ears and body, note things like dry patches or ear buildup, and tell owners what they find. The shop recommends a routine visit every four to six weeks.
Owners who prefer to wash their own dog can use the self-wash stations, which come with tubs, towels, shampoo and dryers. The shop is open Tuesday through Sunday from 10am to 6pm and closed Mondays.

name: Dave & Buster's Alpharetta
desc: Big arcade and sports bar near North Point Mall with 100-plus games, from racing and shooting games to air hockey and basketball, plus newer attractions like high-tech darts, Social Shuffle and The Arena. Large HD screens show games, and the full restaurant and bar serves food, craft beer and cocktails.
tips: Plan around happy hour, weekdays 4pm to 7pm or late evenings Sunday to Thursday
Call (678) 256-1100 to reserve a table for a group
Look at the Eat and Play combos before buying a Power Card
about: Dave & Buster's Alpharetta combines an arcade, sports bar and restaurant at 6500 North Point Parkway. The game floor has more than 100 games, including newer attractions like High-Tech Darts and Social Shuffle, which groups of up to six can play together.

Sports fans can watch NFL, college football, basketball, hockey and UFC on large HDTVs, including 40-foot screens, with a full-service bar and menu. Game play runs on Power Cards, and combo deals pair an entree with a card or an unlimited play upgrade.

Happy hour runs Monday through Friday from 4pm to 7pm and again Sunday through Thursday from 9pm to 11pm, with discounted cocktails, drafts and house wine. Tables can be reserved by phone for events and parties.

name: Activate Alpharetta
desc: Active gaming venue where groups of two to five move through themed rooms like Grid, Mega Laser, Climb, Hoops and Strike, playing short 1 to 3 minute challenges across 10 difficulty levels. Electronic wristbands track every score for a global leaderboard. It is physically demanding, with running, jumping and climbing.
tips: Book online ahead of time; walk-ins are welcome but not guaranteed
Solo players cannot play, so bring at least one other person
Guests ages 6 to 13 need an adult in the building for the whole session
about: Activate Alpharetta is an active gaming venue at 3020 Windward Place where teams move through themed game rooms that use the whole body instead of a controller. Rooms include Hoops, Grid, Mega Grid, Climb, Mega Laser, Control, Strike and Scan, with challenges such as a lava floor of colored tiles, a laser maze and a climbing wall with landmines.

Games are built for groups of two to five, and larger groups split into teams and rotate. The activity is physically demanding, with running, jumping, climbing and throwing, and rooms use flashing lights, fog and loud music.
The minimum age is 6, and games can be hard for kids under 10. Hours are noon to 10pm Monday through Thursday, 10am to 11pm on Friday and Saturday, and 10am to 10pm on Sunday.

name: All Fired Up Alpharetta
desc: Paint-your-own pottery studio on Main Street with hundreds of pieces to choose from, including mugs, plates, bowls and kids' items. There is no studio fee: you pay for the piece, and paint, brushes, glazing and firing are included. It also runs clay hand-building, themed workshops, date nights and birthday parties.
tips: Reserve for weekends and holidays; a $25 deposit holds your table and goes toward your bill
Book online at least 72 hours ahead, or call for anything sooner
Groups of six or more should call the studio to plan their visit
about: All Fired Up is a paint-your-own pottery studio at 53 South Main Street in downtown Alpharetta. Visitors choose from more than 700 pieces, including mugs, plates, bowls, figurines, home decor and kids' designs, and paint them with the studio's colors.

There are no studio or sitting fees; you pay for the piece you pick, and paints, brushes and supplies are provided. Specialty glazes cost extra. No experience is needed, and staff help first-timers get started. The studio also offers clay hand-building, guided workshops, date nights and parties for kids, teens and adults.
Hours are 10am to 8pm Monday through Thursday, 10am to 10pm on Friday and Saturday, and noon to 7pm on Sunday.

name: The Scene Art Gallery
desc: Gallery run by the nonprofit Alpha Arts Guild on the second level of North Point Mall, showing and selling work by Georgia artists. It has about 6,000 square feet of exhibit space plus 5,000 square feet for workshops and open studio time, and hosts a monthly Spotlight Show reception with a collaborative Paint Around session.
tips: Hours are not posted online, so email info@thesceneartgallery.org before visiting
Browse the online member showcase to see artists' work in advance
Ask about Guild membership if you are a Georgia artist looking for exhibition opportunities
about: The Scene Art Gallery at North Point Mall is run by the Alpha Arts Guild, a 501(c)(3) nonprofit founded in 2008 to support Georgia-based artists. The gallery shows and sells work by local artists and invites the public to engage with the region's creative community.

Guild members work in oils, acrylics, sculpture, photography, textile arts, mixed media and more. Through the gallery and the Guild, members take part in juried shows, exhibitions, lectures and workshops, and the Guild brings in established art professionals to work with emerging artists. Hobbyists and art lovers can join as members or volunteers.
The Guild's online member showcase lets visitors browse individual artists' galleries and contact them directly about buying a piece.

name: Spa Sydell Alpharetta
desc: Alpharetta location of the Atlanta-based integrative aesthetics spa, which also has Buckhead and Perimeter studios. Services range from facials, chemical peels, microneedling and massage to injectables, CoolSculpting, Ultherapy and the triLift non-surgical facelift, along with wellness programs such as peptide and hormone therapy.
tips: Enter Old Alabama Road Connector in your GPS, not just Old Alabama Road
Call (404) 255-7727 and press extension 3 for the Alpharetta spa
Book ahead for holidays, when appointments fill quickly

about: Spa Sydell's Alpharetta studio is at 10593 Old Alabama Road Connector, in a shopping plaza that also includes Jazzercise and Brimstone Tavern. The Atlanta integrative aesthetics company also has locations in Buckhead and Perimeter.

Treatment menus cover facials, microneedling, laser facials and massage, along with injectables, CoolSculpting, Ultherapy and the triLift non-surgical facelift. The company also offers wellness programs that include peptide therapy and memberships at several levels.

Free parking sits right in front of the building, and the suite is easy to reach from the main lot. Hours are posted on the company's locations page. Appointments can be booked online or by calling the main line at (404) 255-7727 and choosing extension 3 for Alpharetta.

name: The Lash Lounge Alpharetta - Old Alabama Square
desc: Lash and brow salon in Old Alabama Square near The Fresh Market, with a calm, spa-like setting. Services include classic, wet and spiky lash extensions, LED-cured lashes, fills, lash lifts, brow lamination, threading, tinting and permanent makeup, and memberships are available for regular fill appointments.
tips: First-time guests can claim savings on a first full set through the website

about: The Lash Lounge Alpharetta is a lash and brow salon in Old Alabama Square, next to The Fresh Market. The spa-like salon is set up for relaxation, with cozy blankets and calm music, and it draws guests from Roswell and Johns Creek as well as Alpharetta.

Services include custom lash extensions, Purple Light LED lash extensions that cure the bond in under four seconds, lash lifts and tinting, brow lamination, threading and tinting. Every extension appointment begins with a one-on-one consultation to design a look, and regular fills are needed about every two weeks as natural lashes shed.

The Lash Lounge brand was founded by Anna Phillips, and its stylists finish weeks of company training before earning certification. Memberships are available for guests who keep a regular fill schedule.

name: [solidcore] Avalon
desc: Boutique studio next to Lululemon at Avalon teaching 50-minute, high-intensity, low-impact resistance classes on a machine, using slow, controlled movements that work the core, legs and upper body. Classes are small so coaches can give hands-on cues, and beginner formats like Starter50 explain the machine and pace the rest.
tips: Park in the garage near Westside Parkway and 1st Street, by the Tesla Superchargers
Book classes in advance through the studio page
Read the FAQ before your first class so you know what to bring
about: [solidcore] Avalon is a boutique fitness studio at 5199 Avalon Boulevard, next to Lululemon and across the street from Rumi's Kitchen. It teaches a high-intensity, low-impact workout inspired by Pilates on a custom-built reformer machine.

Workouts take place on the reformer, and the brand rotates a monthly muscle focus so classes emphasize different areas over time. Coaches guide each class, and the company offers options for pregnancy and postpartum clients along with a frequently asked questions page for new members.

Classes are booked online through the studio page, where the weekly schedule, pricing and packages are also listed. The Avalon location also has a head coach and community manager on staff, and newcomers can sign up for text updates about offers. The studio phone is (770) 692-0685.

name: Ed Isakson / Alpharetta Family YMCA
desc: Full-service family Y with indoor and outdoor pools, a climbing wall, gym and indoor basketball, a wellness center and group exercise classes. It runs swim lessons and a swim team, youth sports, dance, gymnastics and martial arts, summer and school-break camps, and the largest afterschool program in north Georgia.
tips: Use the play center childcare while you work out
Day passes and financial assistance are available through YMCA of Metro Atlanta
Check the pool schedules online before you go
about: The Ed Isakson / Alpharetta Family YMCA at 3655 Preston Ridge Road serves families from Alpharetta, Roswell, Milton and nearby communities. It is part of the YMCA of Metro Atlanta and runs the largest afterschool program in north Georgia.

Facilities include an indoor pool, an outdoor pool, a climbing wall and a gymnasium, along with wellness areas and group exercise. Swim programs range from lessons and adaptive swim to a swim team, and camps include day camp, school break camp and overnight options through the wider Y. A play center provides childcare while parents work out.

The Y works with local government, businesses and community groups on programs for youth, families and older adults. Hours are 5am to 9pm Monday through Thursday, 5am to 8pm Friday, 7am to 6pm Saturday and 8am to 5pm Sunday.
